learn.hook: A big train can carry about 1,000 people. How many such trains would fill one lakh seats? Let's find out!
points: 10 hundreds make 1 thousand (1,000).
10 thousands make ten thousand (10,000).
10 ten-thousands make 1 lakh (1,00,000). A lakh has 5 zeros and 6 digits.
In India we put the first comma after 3 digits from the right, then after every 2 digits: 2,45,630.
We read 2,45,630 as 'two lakh forty-five thousand six hundred thirty'.

example.q: How many ₹100 notes make ₹1 lakh?

learn.reallife: Prices of scooters, the number of people in a city and cricket stadium crowds are often in thousands or lakhs.

games.title: True or false?
items: 3,45,200 has its commas in the right places the Indian way.
First comma after 3 digits from the right, then after 2 digits.
Add 1 and you get 1,00,000, which has 6 digits.
1,00,000 is a 1 followed by 5 zeros: 6 digits.

quiz.q: How many zeros are there in 1 lakh written as a number?
quiz.explain: 1 lakh is 1,00,000: a 1 followed by 5 zeros.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up a lakh with ten thousand (4 zeros) or ten lakh (6 zeros)

quiz.q: How many thousands make 1 lakh?
quiz.mistake: Thinks 10 thousands make a lakh (10 thousands make only 10,000)

quiz.q: Write 'three lakh six thousand forty' in numbers.
quiz.explain: 3 lakh = 3,00,000, six thousand = 6,000, forty = 40. Together: 3,06,040. The ten-thousands place is 0.
quiz.mistake: Puts the 6 in the ten-thousands place or the 4 in the hundreds place

quiz.q: How do we read 4,52,309?
options: Four lakh five thousand two hundred thirty-nine
Four lakh fifty-two thousand three hundred ninety
Four lakh fifty-two thousand three hundred nine
quiz.explain: 4 lakh, then 52 thousand, then 309 (three hundred nine).
quiz.mistake: Reads the digits in the wrong groups or reads 09 as ninety

quiz.q: A stadium has 10 stands. Each stand seats 10,000 fans. How many fans can sit in all?
quiz.explain: 10 groups of 10,000 make 1,00,000, which is 1 lakh.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to multiply by 10, or adds an extra zero

quiz.q: Which number comes just after 99,999?
quiz.explain: 99,999 + 1 = 1,00,000. It is the first 6-digit number.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the number after 99,999 is still a 5-digit number

quiz.q: Arjun has 4 bundles of ₹10,000 and 5 notes of ₹1,000. How much money does he have?
quiz.mistake: Writes the digits side by side without thinking of place value

quiz.q: What is the smallest 6-digit number?
quiz.explain: The smallest 6-digit number is 1 followed by five zeros: 1,00,000.
quiz.mistake: Picks the largest 5-digit number instead

teach.ask: Gappu flaps: 'What is a lakh? How big is it?'
teach.praise: Wow! Now I know a lakh is 100 thousand. That's a lot of seeds!
teach.nudge: But how many zeros does a lakh have? And how is it made from ten thousands?

learn.hook: The same digit 5 can be worth 5 rupees or 5 lakh rupees. Its place decides!
points: Places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, lakhs.
Each place is worth 10 times the place on its right.
Place value = digit × value of its place. In 3,72,915 the 7 is worth 70,000.
Expanded form breaks a number into place values: 3,72,915 = 3,00,000 + 70,000 + 2,000 + 900 + 10 + 5.
A zero keeps a place empty: in 4,05,000 there are no ten thousands.

example.q: What is the place value of 7 in 3,72,915?
steps: Count places from the right: 5 ones, 1 ten, 9 hundreds, 2 thousands, 7 ten thousands

learn.reallife: Bank slips, cheques and price tags use place value. A shopkeeper knows ₹50,000 and ₹5,000 are very different!

items.text: In 9,07,560 the digit in the thousands place is ___
1 lakh = ___ ten thousands
The place just left of ten thousands is ___

quiz.q: In 5,38,214, which digit is in the ten thousands place?
quiz.explain: From the right: 4 ones, 1 ten, 2 hundreds, 8 thousands, 3 ten thousands, 5 lakhs.
quiz.mistake: Counts places from the left instead of the right

quiz.q: What is the place value of 6 in 2,64,105?
quiz.explain: 6 is in the ten thousands place, so it is worth 6 × 10,000 = 60,000.
steps: 6 is in the ten thousands place
quiz.mistake: Gives the face value 6 or picks the wrong place

quiz.q: What is the place value of 4 in 4,12,380?
quiz.explain: The 4 is in the lakhs place: 4 × 1,00,000 = 4,00,000.
quiz.mistake: Stops counting places one place too early

quiz.q: Write 3,00,000 + 50,000 + 700 + 9 as one number.
quiz.explain: 3 lakhs, 5 ten thousands, 0 thousands, 7 hundreds, 0 tens, 9 ones: 3,50,709.
steps: Lakhs 3, ten thousands 5, thousands 0, hundreds 7, tens 0, ones 9
quiz.mistake: Forgets to put zeros in the empty places

quiz.q: Kabir's fair had 2,07,450 visitors. What does the 0 just after the 2 tell us?
quiz.explain: The digit after the lakhs digit is in the ten thousands place. 0 there means no ten thousands.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the ten thousands and thousands places

quiz.q: What is the place value of 3 in 7,85,312?
quiz.explain: 3 is in the hundreds place: 3 × 100 = 300.
quiz.mistake: Gives just the digit instead of its place value

quiz.q: Which number has 9 in the thousands place?
quiz.explain: In 1,29,450 the places from the right are 0 ones, 5 tens, 4 hundreds, 9 thousands.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the thousands place with the ten thousands or hundreds place

quiz.q: 5,25,000 has two 5s. What is the difference between their place values?
quiz.explain: One 5 is in the lakhs place (5,00,000) and the other in the thousands place (5,000). 5,00,000 − 5,000 = 4,95,000.
quiz.mistake: Thinks two same digits always have the same value

teach.ask: Gappu tilts his head: 'Why is the 7 in 70,000 worth more than the 7 in 700?'
teach.praise: Tweet! The place of a digit decides its value. Got it!
teach.nudge: But what makes the same digit worth more? Where is it sitting?

learn.hook: Two trains carried 1,45,300 and 1,54,030 people in a month. Which was busier? Be a number detective!
points: A number with more digits is bigger: 1,00,000 > 99,999.
If the digits are the same in number, compare from the left, place by place.
The first place where the digits differ decides which number is bigger.
Use > for 'greater than', < for 'less than' and = for 'equal to'.
To make the largest number from digits, put them from biggest to smallest.

example.q: Which is more: 1,45,300 or 1,54,030?

learn.reallife: We compare large numbers when we check which city has more people or which phone costs more.

games.title: Smallest to largest
games.prompt: Put the numbers from smallest to largest

quiz.q: Which is greater: 98,765 or 1,02,345?
quiz.explain: 1,02,345 has 6 digits and 98,765 has only 5, so 1,02,345 is greater.
quiz.mistake: Looks only at the first digit (9 > 1) and forgets to count digits

quiz.q: Which symbol goes in the box? 3,45,620 ☐ 3,45,260
quiz.explain: Lakhs, ten thousands and thousands match. In the hundreds, 6 > 2, so 3,45,620 > 3,45,260.
quiz.mistake: Compares from the right side instead of the left

quiz.q: Which is the largest?
quiz.explain: All have 4 lakhs. In the ten thousands place, only 4,10,000 has a 1, so it is the largest.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the number with the most 9s is always largest

quiz.q: Harpreet puts 56,000; 5,60,000 and 5,06,000 in order from smallest. Which is in the middle?
quiz.explain: 56,000 is smallest (5 digits). Then 5,06,000, then 5,60,000.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 5,60,000 and 5,06,000 are the same because they use the same digits

quiz.q: What is the largest 6-digit number made with 3, 0, 7, 1, 9, 5 (each used once)?
quiz.explain: Put the digits from biggest to smallest: 9, 7, 5, 3, 1, 0 gives 9,75,310.
quiz.mistake: Does not put every digit in biggest-to-smallest order

quiz.q: What is the smallest 6-digit number made with 4, 0, 2, 8, 6, 1 (each used once)?
quiz.explain: A number cannot start with 0, so start with 1, then 0, 2, 4, 6, 8: 1,02,468.
quiz.mistake: Does not put the 0 right after the first digit

quiz.q: A number is between 2,99,000 and 3,01,000. Its lakhs digit is 3. Which could it be?
quiz.explain: 3,00,500 has 3 lakhs and lies between 2,99,000 and 3,01,000. 3,01,500 and 3,10,000 are too big.
quiz.mistake: Checks only one of the two clues

quiz.q: Joseph says 89,999 is greater than 1,00,000 because 8 and 9 are big digits. What is the mistake?
options: You must compare the last digits
1,00,000 has more digits, so it is greater
quiz.explain: First count digits. 1,00,000 has 6 digits and 89,999 has 5, so 1,00,000 is greater.
quiz.mistake: Compares the first digits before counting how many digits each number has

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How do I know which big number is bigger?'
teach.praise: Chirp chirp! Count digits first, then compare from the left. Easy!
teach.nudge: What should I check first? And from which side should I compare?

learn.hook: Riya cuts her roti into 4 pieces and eats 2. Arjun cuts his into 8 and eats 4. Who ate more? Surprise: the same!
points: A fraction is a part of a whole cut into equal parts. 3/4 means 3 of 4 equal parts.
The top number is the numerator. The bottom number is the denominator.
Equivalent fractions show the same amount: 1/2 = 2/4 = 3/6 = 4/8.
Multiply the top and the bottom by the same number to get an equivalent fraction.
Equivalent fractions sit on the same spot on a number line.

example.q: Riya eats 2/4 of a roti. Arjun eats 4/8 of the same size roti. Who ate more?

learn.reallife: When you share a pizza or a chikki bar, cutting it into more pieces does not change how much you get.

games.title: True or false?
items: 5/10 is 5 of 10 parts, which is half.
2/4 is half, but 2/8 is only a quarter.
Adding the same number to the top and bottom always gives an equivalent fraction.
1/2 → 2/3 by adding 1, but 2/3 is not half.
Multiplying top and bottom by the same number gives an equivalent fraction.
All 3 of the 3 parts make the whole.

quiz.q: Which fraction is equal to 1/2?
quiz.explain: 3/6 means 3 of 6 equal parts. That is half of the whole.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a fraction with a 1 or 2 in it must be half

quiz.q: A chikki bar has 8 equal pieces. Meena eats 2. What fraction did she eat, in simplest form?
quiz.explain: 2 of 8 is 2/8. Divide top and bottom by 2: 1/4.
quiz.mistake: Counts eaten pieces against pieces left (2/6)

quiz.q: 3/4 = ?/12. What number goes in the box?
quiz.explain: 4 × 3 = 12, so multiply the top by 3 too: 3 × 3 = 9.
quiz.mistake: Changes only the bottom number

quiz.q: Kabir says 2/3 = 4/9 because 2 × 2 = 4 and 3 × 3 = 9. Is he right?
options: No, he must multiply top and bottom by the same number
quiz.explain: He used × 2 on top but × 3 at the bottom. 2/3 = 4/6 or 6/9, not 4/9.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies top and bottom by different numbers

quiz.q: Which pair of fractions are equivalent?
quiz.explain: 2/5: multiply top and bottom by 2 → 4/10. Same amount.
quiz.mistake: Thinks fractions with the same denominator or the same digits must be equal

quiz.q: Harpreet folds a paper into 3 equal parts and colours 1 part. Then she folds each part in half. How many small parts are coloured now?
quiz.explain: The paper now has 6 small parts. The coloured third is now 2 small parts: 1/3 = 2/6.
quiz.mistake: Thinks folding again does not change the number of coloured pieces

quiz.q: On a number line from 0 to 1, which fraction lands on the same spot as 1/2?
quiz.explain: 5/10 means 5 of 10 equal jumps, which is exactly halfway.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 1/5 or 1/10 is close to 1/2 because they start with 1

quiz.q: 4/5 = 16/?. What number goes in the box?
quiz.explain: 4 × 4 = 16, so multiply the bottom by 4: 5 × 4 = 20.
quiz.mistake: Adds 12 to the bottom because 12 was added to the top

teach.ask: Gappu is puzzled: 'How can 1/2 and 2/4 be the same?'
teach.praise: Yay! Cutting into more pieces but taking more pieces keeps it the same!
teach.nudge: How do I make a new fraction that is the same? What do I do to the top and the bottom?

learn.hook: Why say 12/18 of a laddoo box when you can just say 2/3? Let's make fractions tiny and neat!
points: To simplify, divide the top and the bottom by the same number.
A fraction is in simplest form when no number except 1 divides both top and bottom.
Dividing by the biggest common number gets you there in one step.
Simplifying does not change the amount, only the way we write it.

example.q: Write 12/18 in simplest form.

learn.reallife: Cooks and shopkeepers say 'half a kilo' instead of '500/1000 of a kilo'. Simple is easier!

items.text: To simplify, divide top and bottom by the ___ number

quiz.q: Write 6/8 in simplest form.
quiz.explain: Divide top and bottom by 2: 6 ÷ 2 = 3, 8 ÷ 2 = 4.
quiz.mistake: Divides only the top number

quiz.q: What is 10/15 in simplest form?
quiz.explain: Both 10 and 15 can be divided by 5: 10 ÷ 5 = 2 and 15 ÷ 5 = 3.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 5 from the top and bottom instead of dividing

quiz.q: What is 9/12 in simplest form?
quiz.explain: Both 9 and 12 can be divided by 3: 9/12 = 3/4.
quiz.mistake: Divides the top by 3 but the bottom by a different number

quiz.q: Aisha has 20 marbles. 15 are blue. What fraction is blue, in simplest form?
quiz.explain: 15 of 20 is 15/20. Divide top and bottom by 5: 3/4.
quiz.mistake: Finds the fraction that is NOT blue, or divides wrongly

quiz.q: Which fraction is already in simplest form?
quiz.explain: Only 1 divides both 5 and 7. The others can be divided by 2 or 3.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a fraction with small numbers is always simplest

quiz.q: Joseph divides the top of 8/12 by 4 and the bottom by 2, and gets 2/6. What went wrong?
options: He must divide top and bottom by the same number
He should change only the top
quiz.explain: 8/12 ÷ 4 on both gives 2/3. Using different numbers changes the amount.
quiz.mistake: Divides top and bottom by different numbers

quiz.q: A box had 18 laddoos. 12 were eaten at a Diwali party. What fraction was eaten, in simplest form?
quiz.explain: 12/18. Divide both by 6: 2/3.
quiz.mistake: Writes the fraction of laddoos left (1/3) instead of eaten

quiz.q: To simplify 16/24 in one step, which is the biggest number that divides both 16 and 24?
quiz.explain: 8 divides 16 (2 times) and 24 (3 times). No bigger number divides both. 16/24 = 2/3.
quiz.mistake: Picks a common number that is not the biggest

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How do I make 6/9 simpler?'
teach.praise: Neat! Divide top and bottom by the same number. 6/9 is 2/3!
teach.nudge: What do I do to the numbers? And do I do it to both of them?

learn.hook: Would you rather have 1/3 of a big cake or 1/5 of it? Think before you answer!
points: Same bottom number: the bigger top number is bigger. 5/7 > 3/7.
Same top number: the smaller bottom number is bigger, because the pieces are bigger. 1/3 > 1/5.
Different bottoms: make equivalent fractions with the same bottom, then compare.
Using 1/2 as a helper: 5/8 is more than half, 3/8 is less than half.

example.q: Riya eats 2/3 of a cake. Arjun eats 3/4 of the same size cake. Who eats more?

learn.reallife: When friends share sweets, rotis or a cricket field for practice, comparing fractions keeps it fair.

games.title: Smallest to largest
games.prompt: Arrange the fractions from smallest to largest

quiz.q: Which is bigger: 3/7 or 5/7?
quiz.explain: The pieces are the same size (sevenths). 5 pieces are more than 3 pieces.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the fractions are equal because the bottoms match

quiz.q: Which is bigger: 1/3 or 1/5?
quiz.explain: Cutting into 3 gives bigger pieces than cutting into 5. So 1/3 > 1/5.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a bigger bottom number means a bigger fraction

quiz.q: Riya ate 2/3 of a dosa. Kabir ate 3/4 of the same size dosa. Who ate more?
quiz.explain: 2/3 = 8/12 and 3/4 = 9/12. 9/12 is more, so Kabir ate more.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 2/3 and 3/4 are equal because each is one piece short of a whole

quiz.q: Which fraction is more than 1/2?
quiz.explain: Half of 8 is 4. 5/8 has 5 parts, more than 4, so it is more than half.
quiz.mistake: Picks a fraction with a big denominator

quiz.q: Put 3/8, 1/2 and 1/4 in order from smallest. Which is in the middle?
quiz.explain: In eighths: 1/4 = 2/8, 3/8, 1/2 = 4/8. So 3/8 is in the middle.
quiz.mistake: Orders by the bottom numbers only

quiz.q: Meena drank 5/6 of a glass of lassi. Aisha drank 7/12 of the same glass. Who drank more?
quiz.explain: 5/6 = 10/12. 10/12 is more than 7/12, so Meena drank more.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the fraction with bigger numbers (7/12) is bigger

quiz.q: Which is the largest: 2/3, 3/5 or 1/2?
quiz.mistake: Picks the fraction with the biggest top number

quiz.q: In a race, Arjun has run 3/10 of the track and Harpreet has run 2/5. Who is ahead?
quiz.explain: 2/5 = 4/10. 4/10 is more than 3/10, so Harpreet is ahead.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 3/10 is more because 3 > 2

teach.ask: Gappu wonders: 'Is 1/4 bigger than 1/3, because 4 is bigger than 3?'
teach.praise: Oh! More pieces means smaller pieces. 1/3 is bigger. Thank you!
teach.nudge: What happens to the size of each piece when we cut into more parts? How do we compare when bottoms are different?

learn.hook: Spin like a top! Every time you turn, you make an angle.
points: An angle tells us how much something has turned.
We measure turns in degrees (°). A full turn is 360°.
A half turn is 180°. A quarter turn is 90°. A three-quarter turn is 270°.
Clockwise means turning the way clock hands move. Anticlockwise is the opposite way.

example.q: Riya faces North and makes a quarter turn clockwise. Which way does she face? How many degrees did she turn?

learn.reallife: A bowler running up, a fan blade, a door opening and a steering wheel all make turns.

items.text: A full turn is ___ degrees.
Two quarter turns make a ___ turn.
Clock hands always turn ___.
Facing North, a quarter turn clockwise makes you face ___.

quiz.q: How many degrees are there in a full turn?
quiz.explain: A full turn brings you back to where you started. It is 360°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a full turn is 100° or confuses it with a half turn

quiz.q: A half turn is how many degrees?
quiz.explain: Half of a full turn: 360° ÷ 2 = 180°.
quiz.mistake: Confuses a half turn with a quarter turn

quiz.q: Arjun faces North and makes a quarter turn clockwise. Which way does he face now?
quiz.explain: Clockwise from North the next direction is East. A quarter turn takes you there.
quiz.mistake: Turns anticlockwise instead of clockwise

quiz.q: How many quarter turns make one full turn?
quiz.explain: Each quarter turn is 90°. 360° ÷ 90° = 4.
quiz.mistake: Thinks two quarters make a whole

quiz.q: The minute hand moves from 12 to 3. How many degrees does it turn?
quiz.explain: 12 to 3 is a quarter of the clock: 3 gaps × 30° = 90°.
steps: Each gap on the clock is 30°
quiz.mistake: Uses the clock number 3 as the angle

quiz.q: Kabir makes a three-quarter turn. How many degrees is that?
quiz.explain: Three quarter turns: 3 × 90° = 270°.
quiz.mistake: Counts only one or two quarter turns

quiz.q: Meena faces East and makes a half turn. Which way does she face now?
quiz.explain: A half turn makes you face the opposite way. Opposite of East is West.
quiz.mistake: Makes only a quarter turn

quiz.q: The minute hand goes from 12 to 6. What kind of turn is this?
quiz.explain: 12 to 6 is halfway round the clock. That is a half turn, 180°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 6 numbers means a quarter turn

teach.ask: Gappu spins and gets dizzy: 'What is an angle?'
teach.praise: Wheee! An angle is how much I turn. A full turn is 360 degrees!
teach.nudge: But what does an angle measure? How do we count how big the turn is?

learn.hook: The corner of your notebook is a secret angle checker. Let's use it!
points: A right angle is a quarter turn, 90°. It looks like a square corner.
An acute angle is less than a right angle (less than 90°). It looks sharp.
An obtuse angle is more than 90° but less than 180°. It looks wide open.
A straight angle is 180°. Its two arms make a straight line.
Test an angle with the corner of a page: does it fit inside, match, or stick out?

example.q: What kind of angle is 125°?

learn.reallife: Look for angles in a slice of pizza (acute), a door corner (right) and a reclining chair (obtuse).

games.title: True or false?
items: A right angle is a quarter turn.
A quarter turn is 90°, which is a right angle.
An acute angle is bigger than a right angle.
Its arms make a straight line, a half turn.
The corner of a square is an obtuse angle.
Each corner of a square is a right angle.

quiz.q: What kind of angle is 45°?
quiz.explain: 45° is less than 90°, so it is acute.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any angle that is not tiny is right or obtuse

quiz.q: Which angle is obtuse?
quiz.explain: 150° is more than 90° and less than 180°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 180° is obtuse, but it is a straight angle

quiz.q: The corner of a notebook page makes which kind of angle?
quiz.explain: A page corner is a square corner, 90°. That is a right angle.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the names right and acute

quiz.q: What kind of angle is 179°?
quiz.explain: 179° is more than 90° and just less than 180°, so it is obtuse.
quiz.mistake: Thinks an angle very close to 180° is straight

quiz.q: At 3 o'clock, what kind of angle do the clock hands make?
quiz.explain: From 12 to 3 is 3 × 30° = 90°, a right angle.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that 3 gaps on a clock make a quarter turn

quiz.q: At 1 o'clock, what kind of angle do the clock hands make?
quiz.explain: From 12 to 1 is 30°, which is less than 90°. It is acute.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every clock angle is a right angle

quiz.q: At 5 o'clock, the smaller angle between the hands is 150°. What kind of angle is it?
quiz.explain: 150° is between 90° and 180°, so it is obtuse.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up acute and obtuse

quiz.q: Harpreet says every angle bigger than 90° is obtuse. Is she right?
options: No, an obtuse angle must also be less than 180°
No, obtuse angles are less than 90°
quiz.explain: Obtuse angles are between 90° and 180°. 180° is a straight angle, so 'bigger than 90°' is not enough.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the upper limit of 180° for obtuse angles

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How do I tell acute, right and obtuse angles apart?'
teach.praise: Super! Smaller than 90 is acute, exactly 90 is right, bigger is obtuse!
teach.nudge: What number do we compare with? What makes an angle acute and what makes it obtuse?

topics.title: Angles on clocks and in shapes

learn.hook: Your wall clock is a giant angle machine. Every number is a hidden 30° jump!
points: A clock face has 12 equal gaps. 360° ÷ 12 = 30°, so each gap is 30°.
To find the angle between the hands at an o'clock time, count gaps and multiply by 30°.
In 5 minutes the minute hand moves one gap, which is 30°.
Letters and shapes have angles too: L has a right angle, V has an acute angle, a rectangle has 4 right angles.

example.q: What is the angle between the clock hands at 4 o'clock? What kind of angle is it?

learn.reallife: Clock hands, scissors, a ladder against a wall and the hands of a cricket umpire show angles every day.

items.q: Angle between the hands at 3 o'clock
Angle between the hands at 4 o'clock

games.title: Smallest to largest
games.prompt: Put these angles from smallest to largest

quiz.q: On a clock face, how many degrees is the turn from one number to the next?
quiz.explain: A full turn is 360° and there are 12 gaps. 360° ÷ 12 = 30°.
quiz.mistake: Divides by the wrong number or uses 12 as the angle

quiz.q: What is the angle between the clock hands at 2 o'clock?
quiz.explain: From 12 to 2 is 2 gaps: 2 × 30° = 60°.
quiz.mistake: Counts only one gap or multiplies by 10

quiz.q: What is the angle between the clock hands at 6 o'clock?
quiz.explain: From 12 to 6 is 6 gaps: 6 × 30° = 180°. The hands make a straight line.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the hands at 6 make a right angle

quiz.q: The minute hand turns clockwise from 12 to 9. How many degrees does it turn?
quiz.explain: 12 to 9 clockwise is 9 gaps: 9 × 30° = 270°, a three-quarter turn.
quiz.mistake: Measures the short way back (90°) instead of the clockwise turn

quiz.q: Which capital letter has a right angle?
quiz.explain: L has a straight up line meeting a flat line, making a square corner.
quiz.mistake: Thinks curved letters have angles

quiz.q: How many right angles does a rectangle have?
quiz.explain: Every corner of a rectangle is a square corner, and it has 4 corners.
quiz.mistake: Thinks only a square has right angles

quiz.q: In 20 minutes, through how many degrees does the minute hand turn?
quiz.explain: 20 minutes is 4 gaps of 5 minutes. 4 × 30° = 120°.
quiz.mistake: Uses minutes as degrees

quiz.q: Joseph opens a book flat so the two covers make a straight line. What is the angle between them?
quiz.explain: A straight line is a half turn, which is 180°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a flat open book is a right angle or a full turn

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How can a clock tell me about angles?'
teach.praise: Tick-tock! Each gap is 30 degrees, so I count gaps and multiply. Brilliant!
teach.nudge: How many degrees is one gap on the clock? How do I use the gaps?

learn.hook: Two trains together travel thousands of kilometres in a month. Can you add like a station master?
points: Write the numbers one below the other: ones under ones, tens under tens, and so on.
Add from the right. If a column makes 10 or more, carry 1 to the next place on the left.
To subtract, start from the right. If the top digit is smaller, borrow 1 from the next place.
Check a subtraction by adding: answer + the number taken away = the starting number.

example.q: A train covered 24,365 km in March and 18,790 km in April. How far did it go in both months?

When a column adds up to 10 or more, we carry 1 to the next place on the left.

quiz.q: Riya's school collected ₹12,450 on Monday and ₹8,675 on Tuesday for a fair. How much in all?

quiz.mistake: Changes only one zero, or adds 1 instead of taking away

quiz.mistake: Drops a carry when adding three numbers

quiz.mistake: Gives the amount spent (₹2,615) instead of the amount left

quiz.explain: Adding the answer to the number taken away should give back the starting number. 35,730 + 27,480 = 63,210, so she is right.
quiz.mistake: Does not know that adding undoes subtracting

teach.ask: Gappu flaps: 'How do I add two really big numbers without getting muddled?'
teach.praise: Hooray! Line up the places, add from the right and carry when it is 10 or more!

learn.hook: A bus does 24 trips a day. Each trip is 135 km. Can you find the distance in a day without a calculator?
points: To multiply by 10, 100 or 1,000, write 1, 2 or 3 zeros at the end: 45 × 100 = 4,500.
To multiply by a 2-digit number, split it: 135 × 24 = 135 × 20 + 135 × 4.
Division shares a number into equal parts or makes equal groups.
Check a division by multiplying: 2,400 ÷ 8 = 300 because 300 × 8 = 2,400.
A remainder is what is left over. It is always smaller than the number you divide by.

example.q: A bus makes 24 trips a day. Each trip is 135 km. How far does it go in a day?

quiz.mistake: Drops a zero while dividing

quiz.mistake: Multiplies only by the 2 in 12 and forgets the 10

quiz.mistake: Loses or adds a zero

quiz.mistake: Multiplies by only the 20 or only the 5 and forgets to add both parts

quiz.q: Joseph packs 97 laddoos in boxes of 8. How many full boxes does he get, and how many laddoos are left?

quiz.mistake: Adds 4 instead of multiplying, or forgets a carry

teach.ask: Gappu scratches his head: 'How can I multiply 135 by 24? It is too big!'

learn.hook: Do you need the exact answer to know if ₹1,000 is enough for a trip snack? Often a smart guess is enough!
points: Estimating means finding a quick answer that is close to the real one.
To round to the nearest hundred, look at the tens digit. 5 or more: round up. Less than 5: round down.
To round to the nearest thousand, look at the hundreds digit in the same way.
Round the numbers first, then add or subtract. 4,872 + 3,195 is about 5,000 + 3,000 = 8,000.
An estimate helps us check if an exact answer makes sense.

example.q: Estimate 4,872 + 3,195 by rounding each number to the nearest thousand.
steps: 4,872: hundreds digit is 8, round up to 5,000
3,195: hundreds digit is 1, round down to 3,000

learn.reallife: News reports say 'about 2 lakh people came to the mela'. Shoppers round prices to see if they have enough money.

games.title: True or false?
items: 47 rounded to the nearest ten is 50.
The ones digit is 7, which is 5 or more, so we round up.
349 rounded to the nearest hundred is 400.
The tens digit is 4, less than 5, so it rounds down to 300.
650 rounded to the nearest hundred is 700.
The tens digit is 5, so we round up.
An estimate is always exactly the same as the real answer.
An estimate is close, not exact.

quiz.q: Round 3,462 to the nearest hundred.
quiz.explain: The tens digit is 6, which is 5 or more, so round up to 3,500.
steps: Hundreds digit is 4, tens digit is 6
quiz.mistake: Looks at the wrong digit or always rounds down

quiz.q: Round 67,280 to the nearest thousand.
quiz.explain: The hundreds digit is 2, less than 5, so round down to 67,000.
steps: Thousands digit is 7, hundreds digit is 2
quiz.mistake: Rounds up every time, or rounds to the nearest hundred instead

quiz.q: Estimate 498 + 307 by rounding each number to the nearest hundred.
quiz.explain: 498 is about 500 and 307 is about 300. 500 + 300 = 800.
quiz.mistake: Works out the exact answer (805) instead of estimating

quiz.q: A train carried 3,890 people on Monday and 5,120 on Tuesday. Rounding to the nearest thousand, about how many in all?
quiz.mistake: Gives the exact total (9,010) or rounds 3,890 down

quiz.q: Riya has ₹1,000. She wants toys costing ₹212, ₹395 and ₹289. Round each to the nearest hundred. Does she have enough?
quiz.mistake: Rounds ₹395 or ₹289 the wrong way

quiz.q: Which number rounds to 5,000 when rounded to the nearest thousand?
quiz.explain: 4,725 has hundreds digit 7, so it rounds up to 5,000. 4,450 rounds to 4,000; 5,620 and 5,501 round to 6,000.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any number that starts with 5 rounds to 5,000

quiz.q: Estimate 612 − 289 by rounding each number to the nearest hundred.
quiz.explain: 612 is about 600 and 289 is about 300. 600 − 300 = 300.
quiz.mistake: Rounds 289 down to 200, or gives the exact answer

quiz.q: A school needs 28 buses with 52 seats each. Round both to the nearest ten to estimate the seats.
quiz.explain: 28 is about 30 and 52 is about 50. 30 × 50 = 1,500.
quiz.mistake: Rounds 28 down to 20, or works out the exact answer (1,456)

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How do I round 3,462 to the nearest hundred?'
teach.praise: Yay! Look at the tens digit: 6 is 5 or more, so it goes up to 3,500!
teach.nudge: Which digit should I look at? And when do I go up or down?

learn.hook: How far is your school? A few steps, a few hundred metres or a few kilometres? Let's become distance detectives!
points: We measure short lengths in millimetres (mm) and centimetres (cm), like a pencil or an eraser.
We measure longer lengths in metres (m), like a room, a saree or a cricket pitch.
We measure long distances in kilometres (km), like the road from one town to another.
When you use a ruler, start from the 0 mark. If you start at another mark, subtract.
To find the length of a route, add the lengths of its parts.

example.q: Harpreet walks 350 m from home to the shop and then 450 m from the shop to the park. How far does she walk?

learn.reallife: Road signs show kilometres to the next town. Tailors measure cloth in metres and centimetres.

games.title: Shortest to longest
games.prompt: Put these from shortest to longest

quiz.q: Which unit is best for measuring the length of a pencil?
quiz.explain: A pencil is short, so centimetres fit best.
quiz.mistake: Picks a unit for long distances, or a unit that is not for length

quiz.q: Which unit is best for the distance from Delhi to Agra?
quiz.explain: Towns are far apart, so we use kilometres.
quiz.mistake: Thinks metres are enough for long distances between towns

quiz.q: An eraser lies on a ruler. It starts at the 2 cm mark and ends at the 7 cm mark. How long is it?
quiz.explain: Length = end − start = 7 − 2 = 5 cm.
steps: End mark 7 cm, start mark 2 cm
quiz.mistake: Reads only the end mark and forgets the eraser did not start at 0

quiz.q: Which unit should Meena use to measure the length of her classroom?
quiz.explain: A classroom is a few metres long, so metres fit best.
quiz.mistake: Chooses a unit that is far too small or far too big

quiz.q: Kabir takes 10 steps. Each step is about 50 cm. About how far does he walk?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to change centimetres into metres

quiz.q: Meena's school is 2 km from home. She walks there and back every day. How far does she walk each day?
quiz.explain: There and back is the distance two times: 2 km + 2 km = 4 km.
quiz.mistake: Counts only one way

quiz.q: How many millimetres make 1 centimetre?
quiz.explain: Look at a ruler: each centimetre has 10 small marks. 1 cm = 10 mm.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up mm–cm with cm–m (100)

quiz.q: Which road is the longest?
quiz.explain: 1 km = 1,000 m, which is more than 900 m. 1,500 cm is only 15 m.
quiz.mistake: Looks at the biggest number and ignores the unit

teach.ask: Gappu wants to fly to Grandma's village. He asks: 'How do people measure how far things are?'
teach.praise: Wow! Small things in cm, rooms in metres and far places in km. I'll fly 3 km!
teach.nudge: Which unit would you use for a short thing, and which for a far-away town?

learn.hook: A saree is 550 cm long. Is that more or less than 6 metres? Converting units will tell you!
points: 1 m = 100 cm and 1 cm = 10 mm.
1 km = 1,000 m, so half a kilometre is 500 m.
Big unit to small unit: multiply. 3 m = 3 × 100 = 300 cm.
Small unit to big unit: divide. 4,000 m = 4,000 ÷ 1,000 = 4 km.
Mixed units: 2 m 35 cm = 200 cm + 35 cm = 235 cm.

example.q: Write 4 km 75 m in metres.

learn.reallife: Marathon runners talk about 42 km. Tailors change metres into centimetres to cut cloth.

quiz.q: How many centimetres are there in 3 m?
quiz.mistake: Uses 10 or 1,000 instead of 100

quiz.q: 6 km = ? m
quiz.mistake: Uses 100 instead of 1,000

quiz.q: Write 4 m 8 cm in centimetres.
quiz.mistake: Writes 4 and 8 side by side and forgets that 4 m is 400 cm

quiz.q: Write 2,750 m in km and m.

quiz.mistake: Thinks 1 km 200 m is 1,020 m

quiz.q: Half a kilometre is how many metres?
quiz.mistake: Uses 100 m for 1 km

quiz.q: Kabir cuts a 3 m ribbon into pieces of 25 cm for rakhis. How many pieces does he get?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies 3 × 25 without changing metres into centimetres

teach.nudge: How many metres are in 1 km? What do I do with that number?

learn.hook: Which is longer: 3 km 40 m or 3,400 m? They look alike, but they are not!
points: Before adding, subtracting or comparing, write both distances in the same unit.
1 km 50 m = 1,050 m, not 1,500 m. The 50 sits in the tens and ones places.
Add or subtract the numbers just like ordinary numbers.
Change the answer back to km and m if that is easier to read.

example.q: Harpreet walks 650 m to the bus stop and then rides 3 km 400 m by bus. How far does she travel?

learn.reallife: Train timetables list the distance between stations. Cyclists add up the kilometres of each ride.

games.title: True or false?

3 m = 300 cm, and 250 cm is less than 300 cm.
To add 2 km and 300 m, first write them in the same unit.
2 km = 2,000 m, so the total is 2,300 m.

quiz.q: A train goes from Rampur to Sitapur (64 km) and then from Sitapur to Gopalpur (96 km). How far is Rampur to Gopalpur on this route?
quiz.explain: Add the two parts: 64 + 96 = 160 km.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to carry when adding, or subtracts

quiz.q: Meena walked 1 km 250 m in the morning and 850 m in the evening. How many metres did she walk in all?
quiz.mistake: Adds 250 + 850 and forgets the 1 km

quiz.q: Arjun's school is 2 km from home. He has cycled 1 km 350 m. How much farther must he go?
quiz.mistake: Makes a borrowing slip when subtracting from 2,000

quiz.mistake: Reads 3 km 40 m as 3,400 m

quiz.mistake: Divides 2 by 400 without changing km to m

quiz.q: Kabir's home is 750 m from the cycle shop. He goes to the shop and back home two times in a day. How far does he travel?
quiz.explain: Each round trip is 750 × 2 = 1,500 m. Two round trips: 3,000 m = 3 km.
quiz.mistake: Counts only one round trip, or only one way

quiz.q: Riya has 5 m of lace. She uses 1 m 75 cm to decorate a diya stand. How much lace is left?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts the metres but forgets to borrow for the centimetres

quiz.q: A road sign says 'Jaipur 48 km'. Later another sign says 'Jaipur 19 km'. How far has the car gone between the signs?
quiz.mistake: Adds the two distances instead of finding the difference

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How do I add 1 km 250 m and 850 m?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Change both into metres first, then add: 2,100 m!
teach.nudge: Can I add km and m straight away? What should I do first?

learn.hook: Moo! A cow at Gopal's farm gives 12 litres of milk a day. How much milk in a week? Multiplication is the fastest way!
points: Multiply when you have equal groups: 7 days of 12 litres is 7 × 12.
To multiply by a 2-digit number, split it into tens and ones: 24 × 15 = 24 × 10 + 24 × 5.
Price × quantity gives the total cost: 5 litres at ₹56 a litre is 5 × 56.
The order does not matter: 15 × 24 = 24 × 15.

example.q: A farm has 24 cows. Each cow gives 15 litres of milk a day. How much milk is that?

quiz.q: A cow gives 12 litres of milk a day. How much milk does it give in 7 days?
quiz.explain: 7 equal groups of 12: 12 × 7 = 84 litres.
quiz.mistake: Adds 12 + 7 instead of multiplying

quiz.q: A farm has 24 cows. Each gives 15 litres a day. How many litres in all?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies only by the 5 and forgets the 10

quiz.mistake: Adds 56 + 5 or forgets to carry

quiz.q: A dairy packs 36 paneer cubes in a tray. How many cubes are in 25 trays?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies by only the 20

quiz.explain: 4 rows of 6 is 4 × 6 = 24 bottles.
quiz.mistake: Adds the rows and the bottles in a row

quiz.q: Kabir's cows gave 145 litres on Monday. On Tuesday they gave double that. How much on Tuesday?
quiz.explain: Double means × 2: 145 × 2 = 290 L.
quiz.mistake: Adds 2 instead of multiplying by 2

quiz.q: Which of these is the same as 23 × 14?
quiz.explain: Split 14 into 10 and 4. Multiply 23 by each part and add: 23 × 10 + 23 × 4.
quiz.mistake: Splits the number but multiplies only one part

quiz.q: A milk van carries 18 cans. Each can holds 40 litres. How many litres does the van carry?
quiz.mistake: Forgets the zero in 40

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How can I find the milk from 24 cows if each gives 15 litres?'
teach.praise: Moo-velous! 24 × 15: split 15 into 10 and 5, multiply, add. 360 litres!
teach.nudge: What do I do with equal groups? How can I make 24 × 15 easier?

learn.hook: 156 litres of milk must go into 12-litre cans. How many cans? Division will pour it out neatly!
points: Divide to share equally or to make equal groups.
144 ÷ 6 means: share 144 into 6 equal parts, or how many 6s are in 144.
If it does not share exactly, the extra is the remainder. The remainder is always smaller than the number you divide by.
Check: quotient × divisor + remainder = the number you started with.

example.q: 156 litres of milk is poured into cans of 12 litres. How many cans are filled?

learn.reallife: Dairies pack milk into equal packets. Teachers share sweets equally on Children's Day.

items.text: 100 ÷ 8 = 12 with remainder ___

games.title: True or false?
items: 4 × 7 = 28, so the remainder is 1. A remainder of 5 is too big when dividing by 4.
Dividing a number by 1 leaves it the same.
Sharing nothing among 5 gives each 0. So 0 ÷ 5 = 0.

quiz.q: A dairy has 144 litres of milk. It fills 6 cans equally. How much milk goes in each can?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts or multiplies instead of dividing

quiz.q: 96 eggs are packed in trays of 12. How many trays are needed?
quiz.mistake: Adds or subtracts 12 instead of dividing

quiz.q: 50 laddoos are shared equally among 8 friends. How many does each get, and how many are left?

quiz.mistake: Leaves a remainder bigger than 8, or ignores the leftover

quiz.q: Riya's family earns ₹1,800 for milk over 30 days, the same each day. How much is that per day?
quiz.mistake: Drops a zero while dividing

quiz.q: 130 children go on a dairy trip. Each bus seats 40. How many buses are needed so no one is left behind?
quiz.explain: 130 ÷ 40 = 3 remainder 10. The 10 extra children need one more bus, so 4 buses.
quiz.mistake: Ignores the remainder and says 3 buses

quiz.q: 7 × ? = 84. What is the missing number?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 7 from 84

quiz.q: What is 225 ÷ 5?
quiz.mistake: Makes a slip with the tens

quiz.q: Aisha shares 18 cups of curd equally into 3 baskets. How many cups go in each basket?
quiz.explain: 18 ÷ 3 = 6 cups in each basket.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 3 instead of dividing

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How do I share 156 litres of milk into 12-litre cans?'
teach.praise: Yummy! Divide 156 by 12 to get 13 cans, then check with 12 × 13!
teach.nudge: Which operation shares things equally? And how can I check my answer?

learn.hook: Gopal sells milk, ghee and paneer. Every sale is a little puzzle. Let's solve them step by step!
points: Read the problem slowly. Find what is asked.
Look for clue words: 'each' and 'in all' often mean multiply; 'share equally' means divide.
Some problems need two steps. Do one step at a time.
Check that your answer makes sense.

example.q: Joseph buys 3 litres of milk at ₹58 a litre. He pays with a ₹200 note. How much change does he get?

learn.reallife: Shopping, sharing snacks and planning a picnic all need two-step thinking.

games.title: Multiply or divide?
items: Each friend's part of ₹300 shared by 3

games.title: Solving steps
games.prompt: Put the steps for solving a word problem in order

quiz.q: A farmer gets 48 litres of milk in the morning and 36 litres in the evening. He fills 2-litre bottles. How many bottles?
quiz.explain: Total milk: 48 + 36 = 84 L. Bottles: 84 ÷ 2 = 42.
quiz.mistake: Stops after the first step and gives the total litres

quiz.q: Aisha buys 4 packets of paneer at ₹85 each. She pays ₹500. How much change does she get?
quiz.mistake: Gives the cost instead of the change

quiz.q: A dairy sends 360 litres of milk each day, shared equally among 9 shops. How much does one shop get in 7 days?

quiz.mistake: Does only one of the two steps

quiz.q: There are 6 crates with 24 bottles in each. Which operation finds the total number of bottles?

quiz.mistake: Adds the two numbers given instead of thinking of equal groups

quiz.q: Harpreet has ₹250. A box of ghee costs ₹65. How many boxes can she buy?
quiz.explain: 65 × 3 = 195 and 65 × 4 = 260, which is more than ₹250. So she can buy 3 boxes.
quiz.mistake: Rounds up to 4 even though there is not enough money

quiz.q: A cow eats 8 kg of fodder a day. How much do 5 cows eat in 10 days?
quiz.explain: One day for 5 cows: 8 × 5 = 40 kg. For 10 days: 40 × 10 = 400 kg.

quiz.q: 12 children share 3 boxes of 20 laddoos equally. How many laddoos does each child get?

quiz.q: Kabir says: '126 ÷ 6 = 21. I can check it by working out 21 × 6.' Is he right?

teach.praise: Wonderful! Equal groups to find a total means multiply. Sharing equally means divide!
teach.nudge: What clue words tell me to multiply? Which words tell me to divide?

learn.hook: Look at a rangoli border or a saree edge. The same little design comes again and again. That is a pattern!
points: A repeating pattern has a part that repeats. We call it the core.
Find the core by looking for where the pattern starts again.
Shapes can repeat by kind, colour, size or by turning.
To find a far-away shape, count in cores. In ▲ ● ■ ▲ ● ■ the core has 3 shapes.

example.q: In the pattern ▲ ● ■ ▲ ● ■ …, what is the 10th shape?
steps: The 10th shape is the 1st shape of the next core

learn.reallife: Borders on sarees, bangles, tiles on a floor and beads on a necklace all show repeating patterns.

items.text: A B B A B B A ___

games.title: True or false?
items: A pattern can be made by turning the same shape again and again.
In red, blue, red, blue, …, the 9th colour is blue.
Odd places are red, so the 9th is red.
Nothing repeats. It grows by 2 each time.

quiz.q: What comes next? ▲ ● ▲ ● ▲ ?
quiz.explain: The core is ▲ ●. After ▲ comes ●.
quiz.mistake: Repeats the last shape instead of following the core

quiz.q: What is the core of this pattern? 🔴 🔵 🔵 🔴 🔵 🔵 🔴 🔵 🔵
quiz.explain: 🔴 🔵 🔵 is the part that repeats.
quiz.mistake: Picks only part of the core

quiz.q: In ■ ▲ ● ■ ▲ ● …, what is the 12th shape?
quiz.explain: The core has 3 shapes. 12 ÷ 3 = 4 full cores, so the 12th shape is the last in the core: ●.
quiz.mistake: Counts the shapes one by one and slips

quiz.q: The pattern ⭐ 🌙 🌙 repeats. How many stars are in the first 15 shapes?
quiz.explain: 15 shapes make 15 ÷ 3 = 5 cores. Each core has 1 star, so 5 stars.
quiz.mistake: Counts the moons, or counts all the shapes

quiz.q: Riya's rangoli border goes red, yellow, green, red, yellow, green, … What colour is the 20th tile?
quiz.explain: The core has 3 colours. 20 = 3 × 6 + 2, so the 20th is the 2nd colour: yellow.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to use the remainder to find the place in the core

quiz.q: Each arrow is the one before turned a quarter turn clockwise: ↑ → ↓ ? What comes next?
quiz.explain: A quarter turn clockwise from ↓ (down) points ← (left).
quiz.mistake: Turns anticlockwise or turns a half turn

quiz.q: Kabir strings beads: 2 red, 1 white, 2 red, 1 white, … He uses 18 beads. How many are red?
quiz.explain: Each core has 3 beads, 2 of them red. 18 ÷ 3 = 6 cores. 6 × 2 = 12 red.
quiz.mistake: Thinks half the beads are red

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a repeating pattern?
options: A B A B A B
quiz.explain: 3 5 8 2 9 1 has no part that repeats.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any list of things is a pattern

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'What makes a pattern a repeating pattern?'
teach.praise: Tweet tweet! The core repeats again and again. Like my song!
teach.nudge: What happens again and again in a pattern? What do we call that part?

learn.hook: Make squares with matchsticks in a row. 1 square needs 4 sticks. Does 2 squares need 8? Try it!
points: In a growing pattern, each step changes by a rule.
Find the rule by checking how much it grows each time: 4, 7, 10 grows by 3.
Use the rule to find later steps without drawing everything.
Some patterns grow by adding more each time: 1, 3, 6, 10 adds 2, then 3, then 4.

example.q: Matchstick squares in a row: 1 square uses 4 sticks, 2 squares use 7, 3 squares use 10. How many sticks for 5 squares?
steps: The rule: add 3 sticks for each new square

learn.reallife: Stacks of laddoos, steps of a staircase and seats in a stadium often grow in patterns.

quiz.q: What comes next? 3, 6, 9, 12, ?
quiz.explain: The rule is add 3. 12 + 3 = 15.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 instead of finding the rule

quiz.q: Matchstick squares in a row use 4, 7, 10, … sticks. How many sticks for 6 squares?
quiz.explain: Start with 4 and add 3 for each extra square: 4 + 3 × 5 = 19.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every square needs 4 new sticks (6 × 4 = 24)

quiz.q: Dots make triangles: 1, 3, 6, 10, … What comes next?
quiz.explain: It adds 2, then 3, then 4, so next add 5: 10 + 5 = 15.
quiz.mistake: Adds the same amount every time

quiz.q: Arjun builds towers of 2, 4, 8, 16 blocks. Each tower doubles. How many blocks in the next tower?
quiz.mistake: Adds 2 or adds 8 instead of doubling

quiz.q: Square dot patterns have 1, 4, 9, 16 dots. How many dots in the next square?
quiz.explain: The squares are 1×1, 2×2, 3×3, 4×4. Next is 5×5 = 25.
quiz.mistake: Adds 4 each time

quiz.q: Matchstick triangles in a row: 1 triangle uses 3 sticks, 2 use 5, 3 use 7. How many sticks for 10 triangles?
quiz.explain: Each new triangle adds 2 sticks. 3 + 2 × 9 = 21.
quiz.mistake: Thinks each triangle needs 3 new sticks (10 × 3 = 30)

quiz.q: What is the rule? 5, 9, 13, 17, …
quiz.explain: Each number is 4 more than the one before.
quiz.mistake: Looks only at the first number

quiz.q: Meena counts down: 100, 90, 80, 70, … What is the 8th number?
quiz.explain: Each step takes away 10. The 8th number is 7 steps after 100: 100 − 70 = 30.
quiz.mistake: Takes 8 steps instead of 7

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How can I find the 20th step of a growing pattern without drawing it all?'
teach.praise: Chirpy cheer! Find the rule and use it again and again. No drawing needed!
teach.nudge: What stays the same from one step to the next? How do I use that?

learn.hook: How do tiles cover a whole floor with no gaps? Some shapes are tiling champions!
points: Tiling means covering a flat surface with shapes with no gaps and no overlaps.
Squares, rectangles, equilateral triangles and regular hexagons can tile a floor on their own.
Circles always leave gaps. Regular pentagons also leave gaps.
Where corners meet at a point, they fill a full turn of 360°: 4 squares (4 × 90°), 3 hexagons (3 × 120°) or 6 triangles (6 × 60°).

example.q: A floor is 4 m long and 3 m wide. How many square tiles of side 1 m will cover it?

learn.reallife: Floor tiles, brick walls, honeycombs and chessboards are all tilings.

games.title: Can it tile on its own?
True or false?
items: Squares can cover a floor with no gaps.
Square tiles fit edge to edge, 4 at each corner.
Circles can tile a floor with no gaps.
Round edges always leave gaps between circles.
Bricks in a wall make a tiling of rectangles.
The bricks fit with no gaps and no overlaps.
Tiles in a tiling may overlap.
4 square corners fit exactly around one point.

quiz.q: Which shape cannot tile a floor on its own without gaps?
quiz.explain: Circles have curved edges, so gaps are always left between them.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any shape can tile if you push it close

quiz.q: In a floor of square tiles, how many squares meet at one corner point?
quiz.explain: Each square corner is 90°. 360° ÷ 90° = 4.
quiz.mistake: Does not use the full turn of 360°

quiz.q: Honeybees build their honeycomb with cells of which shape?
quiz.explain: Honeycomb cells are hexagons. They fit together with no gaps.
quiz.mistake: Guesses circle because the cells look round from far

quiz.q: How many regular hexagons meet at one point in a hexagon tiling?
quiz.explain: Each hexagon corner is 120°. 360° ÷ 120° = 3.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the answer is 6 because a hexagon has 6 sides

quiz.q: A floor is 5 tiles long and 4 tiles wide. How many tiles cover it?
quiz.explain: 4 rows of 5 tiles: 5 × 4 = 20.
quiz.mistake: Adds length and width instead of multiplying

quiz.q: In tiling, what does 'no overlaps' mean?
options: Tiles do not sit on top of each other
quiz.explain: Overlap means one tile covers part of another. A tiling has none.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up 'overlap' with 'gap'

quiz.q: How many equilateral triangles meet at one point in a triangle tiling?
quiz.explain: Each corner of an equilateral triangle is 60°. 360° ÷ 60° = 6.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the answer is 3 because a triangle has 3 corners

quiz.q: Aisha's bathroom wall needs 6 rows of 8 tiles. She has 40 tiles. How many more does she need?
quiz.explain: She needs 6 × 8 = 48 tiles. 48 − 40 = 8 more.
quiz.mistake: Gives the total needed instead of how many more

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'What is tiling? Why don't people use round tiles?'
teach.praise: Wow! Tiles must cover with no gaps and no overlaps. Round ones leave gaps!
teach.nudge: What must a tiling never have? What goes wrong with circles?

learn.hook: Which is heavier: a kilo of cotton or a kilo of potatoes? Think carefully before you laugh!
points: Weight tells us how heavy something is.
Light things like a pencil or a coin are weighed in grams (g).
Heavy things like a sack of rice or a child are weighed in kilograms (kg).
On a balance, the heavier side goes down.

example.q: A packet of salt weighs 1 kg. A packet of tea weighs 250 g. How many tea packets weigh the same as the salt?

learn.reallife: Vegetable sellers weigh onions in kg. Sweet shops weigh barfi in grams. (And a kilo of cotton weighs the same as a kilo of potatoes!)

games.title: Lightest to heaviest
games.prompt: Put these from lightest to heaviest

quiz.q: Which unit should we use to weigh a watermelon?
quiz.explain: A watermelon is heavy, so kilograms fit best.
quiz.mistake: Picks grams for a heavy object, or a unit that is not for weight

quiz.q: Which unit should we use to weigh a 1-rupee coin?
quiz.explain: A coin is very light, so grams fit best.
quiz.mistake: Chooses kilograms for everything

quiz.q: On a balance, Riya puts a mango on one side and a lemon on the other. The mango side goes down. What does this tell us?
quiz.explain: The heavier side always goes down.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the side that goes up is heavier

quiz.q: How many grams make 1 kilogram?
quiz.explain: Kilo means thousand. 1 kg = 1,000 g.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up with 1 m = 100 cm

quiz.q: Which is the heaviest?
quiz.explain: 1 kg 50 g = 1,050 g. That is more than 1,005 g and 900 g.
quiz.mistake: Reads 1 kg 50 g as 1,005 g or 1,500 g

quiz.q: 4 packets of dal weigh 250 g each. What is their total weight?
quiz.mistake: Gives the weight of one packet

quiz.q: Kabir weighs 32 kg. His little sister weighs 19 kg. How much heavier is Kabir?
quiz.mistake: Adds the weights instead of finding the difference

quiz.q: A bag holds 5 kg of rice. Meena uses 750 g. How many grams are left?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 750 from 5 without changing kg to g, or slips with borrowing

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'When do I use grams and when do I use kilograms?'
teach.praise: Super! Light things in grams, heavy things in kilograms, and 1 kg is 1,000 g!
teach.nudge: Which unit is for light things? How many grams make a kilogram?

learn.hook: How many glasses of nimbu pani can you pour from one big jug? Capacity has the answer!
points: Capacity is how much a container can hold.
Small amounts like medicine or a spoonful are measured in millilitres (ml).
Bigger amounts like a bottle, bucket or tank are measured in litres (L).
1 L = 1,000 ml, so half a litre is 500 ml.

example.q: A jug holds 1 L of nimbu pani. Each glass holds 200 ml. How many glasses can be filled?

learn.reallife: Milk packets, water bottles, cooking oil and petrol are all sold by capacity.

games.title: True or false?
items: A bucket holds more than a cup.
A bucket holds many litres. A cup holds only a few hundred millilitres.
Milk can be measured in litres or millilitres.
For example a 500 ml packet or a 1 L packet.
Two 500 ml bottles fill a 1 L jug.

items.text: Water in a big tank is measured in ___
4 glasses of 250 ml make ___ L
Half a litre is ___ ml

quiz.q: Which unit should we use for a spoonful of cough syrup?
quiz.explain: A spoonful is a small amount, so millilitres fit best.
quiz.mistake: Uses litres for very small amounts

quiz.q: Which of these holds about 1 litre?
quiz.explain: A common water bottle holds about 1 L.
quiz.mistake: Does not have a sense of how much a litre is

quiz.q: A glass holds 250 ml. How many glasses fill a 1 L jug?
quiz.mistake: Uses 1 L = 100 ml

quiz.q: Arjun drinks 6 glasses of water. Each glass holds 200 ml. How much does he drink?
quiz.explain: 6 × 200 = 1,200 ml, which is 1 L 200 ml.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of multiplying

quiz.q: Jug A holds 750 ml. Jug B holds 1 L. Which jug holds more?
quiz.explain: 1 L = 1,000 ml, which is more than 750 ml.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 750 is bigger than 1 without looking at units

quiz.q: A bucket holds 15 L. A mug holds 500 ml. How many mugs fill the bucket?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to change litres into millilitres

quiz.q: A water tank had 50 L. The family used 18 L. How much is left?
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of subtracting, or borrows wrongly

quiz.q: A 2 L bottle of mango juice is poured into cups of 200 ml. How many cups are filled?
quiz.mistake: Uses 1 L = 100 ml

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'What is capacity? How are millilitres and litres connected?'
teach.praise: Glug glug! Capacity is how much a thing holds, and 1 litre is 1,000 ml!
teach.nudge: What does capacity tell us about a bottle? How many ml make a litre?

learn.hook: Granny's recipe says 1 kg 250 g of flour, but the packet says grams. Let's convert like a chef!
points: kg to g: multiply by 1,000. L to ml: multiply by 1,000.
g to kg: divide by 1,000. ml to L: divide by 1,000.
Mixed units: 2 kg 350 g = 2,000 g + 350 g = 2,350 g.
Half a kg = 500 g and a quarter kg = 250 g. The same works for litres and ml.
To add or subtract, change to the same unit first.

example.q: Add 1 kg 750 g and 2 kg 500 g.

learn.reallife: Recipes, shopping lists and medicine bottles all mix kg, g, L and ml.

quiz.q: 3 kg 450 g = ? g
quiz.mistake: Writes the digits side by side without changing kg to g

quiz.q: Write 7,500 ml in litres and millilitres.
quiz.mistake: Splits the digits in the wrong place

quiz.q: For Diwali, Aisha bought 1 kg 250 g of kaju katli and 750 g of laddoos. What is the total weight?
quiz.mistake: Adds 250 + 750 but forgets the carry into kg

quiz.q: A 1 L bottle has 350 ml of water in it. How much more water will fill it?
quiz.mistake: Makes a slip subtracting from 1,000

quiz.q: Which is heavier: 2,500 g or 2 kg 50 g?
quiz.explain: 2 kg 50 g = 2,050 g, which is less than 2,500 g.
quiz.mistake: Reads 2 kg 50 g as 2,500 g

quiz.q: A shop has 10 kg of sugar. It packs it into 500 g packets. How many packets?
quiz.mistake: Uses 1 kg = 100 g

quiz.q: A cook uses 3 L 200 ml of milk for kheer and 1 L 900 ml for chai. How much milk in millilitres?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to carry when the ml add up to more than 1,000

quiz.q: How many grams are in a quarter of a kilogram?
quiz.explain: 1 kg = 1,000 g. A quarter is 1,000 ÷ 4 = 250 g.
quiz.mistake: Confuses a quarter with a half

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How do I change 3 kg 450 g into grams?'
teach.praise: Brilliant! 3 kg is 3,000 g, and 3,000 + 450 makes 3,450 g!
teach.nudge: How many grams are in each kilogram? What do I do with the 450 g?

learn.hook: Farmer Joseph has a heap of coconuts. Can he put them in neat equal rows with none left over? Let's find out!
points: Grouping means putting things into equal groups or equal rows.
The same number can often be grouped in different ways: 12 = 1 × 12 = 2 × 6 = 3 × 4.
If things do not fit equally, the extra ones are left over (the remainder).
Rows and columns make counting quick: 4 rows of 6 is 24.

example.q: In how many ways can 24 coconuts be put in equal rows? (Count 3 rows of 8 and 8 rows of 3 as the same way.)

learn.reallife: Eggs in trays, chairs in a hall and plants in a garden are all arranged in equal rows.

quiz.q: 18 coconuts are put in rows of 6. How many rows are there?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 6 from 18 instead of dividing

quiz.q: 20 coconuts are packed in bags of 3. How many full bags are there, and how many are left over?
quiz.explain: 3 × 6 = 18, so 6 full bags. 20 − 18 = 2 left.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 3 × 7 = 20, or leaves a remainder bigger than 3

quiz.q: Which way can 15 coconuts be put in equal rows with none left over?
quiz.explain: 3 × 5 = 15 exactly.
quiz.mistake: Picks rows that come close to 15 but are not exact

quiz.q: Riya puts 36 coconuts into 4 equal heaps. How many coconuts are in each heap?
quiz.explain: 36 ÷ 4 = 9 coconuts in each heap.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 4 instead of dividing

quiz.q: In how many different ways can 12 coconuts be put in equal rows? (2 rows of 6 and 6 rows of 2 count as the same.)
quiz.mistake: Counts 2 × 6 and 6 × 2 as different ways

quiz.q: A farmer packs 45 coconuts into boxes. Each box holds 10. How many boxes does he need to pack all of them?
quiz.explain: 4 boxes hold 40. The last 5 coconuts need one more box, so 5 boxes.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the leftover coconuts need a box too

quiz.q: Which number of coconuts can NOT be put in 2 or more equal rows with 2 or more in each row?
quiz.explain: 7 can only be 1 row of 7. 8 = 2 × 4, 9 = 3 × 3 and 10 = 2 × 5.
quiz.mistake: Thinks odd numbers can never make equal rows (but 9 = 3 × 3)

quiz.q: Kabir puts 5 coconuts in each of 8 baskets. He has 3 coconuts left over. How many coconuts did he have?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to add the leftover coconuts

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How can I put 12 seeds in equal rows? Is there only one way?'
teach.praise: Peck peck! 1 × 12, 2 × 6 and 3 × 4. Lots of ways for my 12 seeds!
teach.nudge: Must each row have the same number? Can I do it in more than one way?

learn.hook: Can 16 coconuts be shared equally among 3 friends? Among 4? Factors tell you instantly!
points: A factor divides a number exactly, with nothing left over. 4 is a factor of 12 because 12 ÷ 4 = 3.
Factors come in pairs: 12 = 1 × 12 = 2 × 6 = 3 × 4. So the factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12.
1 is a factor of every number, and every number is a factor of itself.
A number with exactly two factors, 1 and itself, is called a prime number. 7 is prime.

example.q: Find all the factors of 18.
steps: 4 and 5 do not divide 18 exactly; after 3 × 6 the pairs repeat

learn.reallife: Factors help us share sweets equally or arrange chairs in neat rows.

items.text: The factors of 10 are 1, 2, ___ and 10
Every number has ___ as a factor

quiz.q: Which of these is a factor of 20?
quiz.explain: 20 ÷ 5 = 4 with nothing left over.
quiz.mistake: Picks a number that is close to a factor but does not divide exactly

quiz.q: How many factors does 12 have?
quiz.explain: The factors are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12. That is 6 factors.
quiz.mistake: Forgets 1 or the number itself

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a factor of 24?
quiz.explain: 24 ÷ 5 = 4 with 4 left over, so 5 is not a factor.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every small number is a factor

quiz.q: Which list shows all the factors of 15?
quiz.explain: 15 = 1 × 15 = 3 × 5. So the factors are 1, 3, 5 and 15.
quiz.mistake: Forgets 1 and the number itself, or lists a multiple like 30
Subtracts 4 from 36

quiz.q: Arjun wants to share 16 coconuts equally among friends with none left. How many friends could he share with?
quiz.explain: 16 ÷ 8 = 2 exactly. 3, 5 and 6 leave some over.
quiz.mistake: Does not check if the division is exact

quiz.q: Which number has only two factors, 1 and itself?
quiz.explain: 11 can only be 1 × 11, so it is a prime number. 9 = 3 × 3, 15 = 3 × 5, 21 = 3 × 7.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every odd number is prime

quiz.q: What is the biggest factor of 30 that is smaller than 30?
quiz.explain: 30 = 2 × 15, so 15 is a factor. No number between 15 and 30 divides 30 exactly.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the number just before 30 must be a factor

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'What is a factor? Is 4 a factor of 12?'
teach.praise: Yes! 4 goes into 12 exactly, 3 times, with nothing left over. So it is a factor!
teach.nudge: What must happen when I divide by a factor? Is anything left over?

learn.hook: Coconuts are sold in bundles of 6. Can a shop sell exactly 40? Multiples will tell you!
points: Multiples of a number are the answers in its times table: multiples of 6 are 6, 12, 18, 24, …
Multiples go on forever. The first multiple of a number is the number itself.
If 3 is a factor of 12, then 12 is a multiple of 3.
Skip counting gives multiples: counting in 5s gives 5, 10, 15, 20, …

example.q: Write the first 5 multiples of 6.

learn.reallife: Packets of 6 bananas, boxes of 12 eggs and weeks of 7 days all give multiples.

games.title: True or false?
items: Every number is a multiple of itself.
4 × 3 = 12 and 4 × 4 = 16. 15 is not in the 4 times table.
A number has only a few multiples.
1 is a factor of every number.

quiz.q: Which of these is a multiple of 7?
quiz.mistake: Picks numbers with a 7 in them

quiz.q: What is the 5th multiple of 8?
quiz.mistake: Adds 8 + 5, or counts one multiple too many

quiz.q: Which list shows multiples of 4?
quiz.mistake: Mixes up factors and multiples, or picks numbers ending in 4

quiz.q: Coconuts are sold in bundles of 6. Which could be the total number of coconuts sold?
quiz.explain: 42 = 6 × 7. 34, 40 and 50 are not in the 6 times table.
quiz.mistake: Picks an even number without checking the 6 times table

quiz.q: 9 is a factor of 54. So 54 is a ___ of 9.
quiz.explain: 54 = 9 × 6, so 54 is in the 9 times table. It is a multiple of 9.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the words factor and multiple

quiz.q: How many multiples of 5 are there from 1 to 50 (including 50)?
quiz.explain: 5, 10, 15, … 50. That is 50 ÷ 5 = 10 multiples.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to count 50, or counts the 5s in 50 wrongly

quiz.q: Meena counts in 3s starting from 3. Which number will she NOT say?
quiz.explain: 32 is not in the 3 times table: 3 × 10 = 30 and 3 × 11 = 33.
quiz.mistake: Does not check every option

quiz.q: What is the smallest multiple of 9 that is bigger than 50?
quiz.explain: 9 × 5 = 45 is too small. 9 × 6 = 54 is the first one bigger than 50.
quiz.mistake: Picks 63 by skipping a multiple, or 45 which is smaller than 50

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'What is the difference between a factor and a multiple?'
teach.praise: Hurray! A factor goes into a number. A multiple is in its times table and they go on forever!
teach.nudge: Which one goes into a number? Which one do I get from the times table?

learn.hook: Fold a paper butterfly down the middle. Both wings match perfectly! That fold is magic: it is a line of symmetry.
points: A line of symmetry cuts a shape into two halves that match exactly, like mirror images.
If you fold along the line, one half sits exactly on the other.
Some shapes have many lines: a square has 4, an equilateral triangle has 3, a rectangle that is not a square has 2.
A circle has endless lines of symmetry: every line through its centre works.
Some shapes and letters have no line of symmetry, like the letters F and S.

example.q: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
steps: Fold it down the middle (up and down): halves match
Fold it across the middle: halves match
Fold along each of the 2 corner-to-corner lines: halves match

learn.reallife: Rangolis, the Taj Mahal, leaves and butterflies all show lines of symmetry.

games.title: True or false?
items: A square has 4 lines of symmetry.
2 through the middles of the sides and 2 through the corners.
Every rectangle has 4 lines of symmetry.
A rectangle that is not a square has only 2.
The capital letter H has 2 lines of symmetry.
One up-down line and one across line.
A line of symmetry splits a shape into two matching halves.
Fold along it and the halves sit exactly on each other.
The capital letter F has a line of symmetry.
No fold of F makes the two halves match.

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
quiz.explain: A square has 2 lines through the middles of its sides and 2 through its corners: 4 in all.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the corner-to-corner lines

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle that is not a square have?
quiz.explain: Only the up-down and across lines through the middle. The corner-to-corner lines do not work.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a rectangle has the same lines as a square

quiz.q: Which capital letter has a line of symmetry?
quiz.explain: A has an up-down line of symmetry through its middle.
quiz.mistake: Picks a letter that only looks balanced

quiz.q: Which capital letter has NO line of symmetry?
quiz.explain: No fold of S makes the halves match. T, M and U each have an up-down line.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a letter that looks the same after a turn must have a line of symmetry

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does an equilateral triangle (all sides equal) have?
quiz.explain: One line from each corner to the middle of the opposite side: 3 lines.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the up-down line

quiz.q: Riya folds a paper along a line and the two halves match exactly. What is the fold line called?
quiz.explain: A line that splits a shape into two matching halves is a line of symmetry.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the name

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a circle have?
options: Endless, any line through the centre
quiz.explain: Every line through the centre of a circle cuts it into two matching halves.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a circle has only an up-down and an across line

quiz.q: Which capital letter has exactly 2 lines of symmetry?
quiz.explain: H has an up-down line and an across line. A has only an up-down line, E only an across line, and F has none.
quiz.mistake: Counts only one line

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'What is a line of symmetry? How do I find one?'
teach.praise: Flappy flap! Fold along the line and the two halves match. Like my wings!
teach.nudge: What do I do with the paper to test it? What happens to the two halves?

learn.hook: Spin a pinwheel. It looks the same again and again before it finishes one full turn! That is turn symmetry.
points: Some designs look exactly the same after a part of a full turn. This is turn (rotational) symmetry.
Count how many times a design looks the same in one full turn.
A square looks the same 4 times in a full turn, after every 90°.
An equilateral triangle looks the same 3 times (every 120°). A rectangle that is not a square looks the same 2 times (every 180°).
Letters like S, N and Z look the same after a half turn (180°).

example.q: A ceiling fan has 3 equal blades. What is the smallest turn after which it looks the same?
steps: It looks the same 3 times in a full turn

learn.reallife: Fans, wheels, flowers, rangolis and chakra designs show turn symmetry.

games.title: Smallest turn to look the same
True or false?
items: The letter S looks the same after a half turn.
Turn S upside down and it is still S.
The letter A looks the same after a half turn.
After a half turn, A is upside down.
A square looks the same after a quarter turn.
A quarter turn is 90°, and a square looks the same every 90°.
A fan with 3 equal blades looks the same after a 90° turn.
It looks the same every 120°, not 90°.
A rectangle that is not a square looks the same after a half turn.
After 180° the long sides are back in place.

quiz.q: A ceiling fan has 3 equal blades. After what smallest turn does it look the same?
quiz.explain: It looks the same 3 times in one full turn: 360° ÷ 3 = 120°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every shape repeats after a quarter turn

quiz.q: A square looks the same after what smallest turn?
quiz.explain: A square looks the same 4 times in a full turn: 360° ÷ 4 = 90°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a square needs a half turn

quiz.q: Which capital letter looks the same after a half turn?
quiz.explain: Turn N upside down and it is still N. A, T and V end up upside down.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up turn symmetry with a mirror line

quiz.q: How many times does a square look the same during one full turn?
quiz.mistake: Counts only the half turn and full turn

quiz.q: A rectangle that is not a square looks the same after what smallest turn?
quiz.explain: After a quarter turn the long sides stand up, so it looks different. After a half turn (180°) it looks the same.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a rectangle behaves like a square

quiz.q: A flower rangoli has 6 equal petals around the centre. After what smallest turn does it look the same?
quiz.explain: It looks the same 6 times in a full turn: 360° ÷ 6 = 60°.
quiz.mistake: Divides 360 by the wrong number

quiz.q: A star has 5 equal points. How many times does it look the same in one full turn?
quiz.explain: Each point moves to the next point's place, so it looks the same 5 times.
quiz.mistake: Counts the corners inside and outside (10)

quiz.q: Which of these does NOT look the same after a quarter turn (90°)?
options: Rectangle that is not a square
quiz.explain: A long rectangle turned 90° stands on its short side, so it looks different.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all four-sided shapes act like squares

teach.ask: Gappu spins round and round: 'What is turn symmetry?'
teach.praise: Wheee! If a design looks the same before a full turn ends, it has turn symmetry!
teach.nudge: What do I do to the design? What must I see before the full turn is over?

learn.hook: Can you finish half a rangoli so it looks perfect? Let's make designs like an artist!
points: To complete a design with a mirror line, copy each part to the other side of the line.
Each point and its mirror image are the same distance from the line, on opposite sides.
On grid paper, count squares from the line to place the image exactly.
Fold-and-cut paper designs always have a line of symmetry along the fold.

example.q: On grid paper, a dot is 3 squares to the left of an up-down mirror line. Where does its mirror image go?
steps: Same distance from the line: 3 squares
example.answer: 3 squares to the right of the line, in the same row

learn.reallife: Kolam and rangoli artists, tailors and kite makers all build symmetrical designs.
