quiz.q: A dot is 2 squares to the left of an up-down mirror line. Where is its mirror image?
quiz.explain: The image is the same distance away on the other side: 2 squares to the right.
quiz.mistake: Puts the image on the same side, or doubles the distance

quiz.q: Meena folds a paper in half and cuts half a heart along the fold. What does she get when she opens it?
options: A full heart with a line of symmetry
quiz.explain: The fold becomes the line of symmetry, so both halves of the heart match.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the two halves come apart

quiz.q: Riya draws half a butterfly on one side of a mirror line. How should she finish it?
options: Draw the same half again, facing the same way
Draw the mirror image of the half on the other side
quiz.explain: The other half must be the flipped (mirror) copy, so the wings match.
quiz.mistake: Copies the half without flipping it

quiz.q: Which word looks exactly the same in a mirror placed beside it?
quiz.explain: M and O each have an up-down line of symmetry, and MOM reads the same both ways. D and B do not have an up-down line.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a word that reads the same both ways always looks the same in a mirror

quiz.q: Half a design touches an up-down mirror line and is 3 squares wide on its left. When it is completed, how wide is the whole design?
quiz.explain: The other half is also 3 squares wide: 3 + 3 = 6 squares.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to add the mirrored half

quiz.q: A rangoli has 8 equal petals around the centre. How many times does it look the same in one full turn?
quiz.explain: Each petal moves to the next petal's place, 8 times in a full turn.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the 4 main directions

quiz.q: Joseph finishes a symmetrical dot design. The left half has 7 dots and no dot is on the line. How many dots are in the whole design?
quiz.explain: The right half mirrors the left: 7 + 7 = 14 dots.
quiz.mistake: Counts only one half

quiz.q: Harpreet makes a kite shape that is symmetrical about an up-down line. The left edge is 30 cm long. How long is the matching right edge?
quiz.explain: Mirror halves match exactly, so the right edge is also 30 cm.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the mirror half is half or double the size

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How do I finish a design if I only have half of it?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Flip each part to the other side, the same distance from the line. Beautiful!
teach.nudge: How do I copy each part? How far from the line should it go?

learn.hook: Nani wants to sew a lace border all around her quilt. How much lace does she need? That length is the perimeter!
points: Perimeter is the total length of the boundary (the edge all around) of a shape.
To find it, add the lengths of all the sides.
Rectangle: perimeter = length + breadth + length + breadth = 2 × (length + breadth).
Square: all 4 sides are equal, so perimeter = 4 × side.
Perimeter is measured in units of length: cm, m or km.

example.q: Nani's quilt is a rectangle 3 m long and 2 m wide. How much lace goes around it?

learn.reallife: Fences around a field, frames around a photo and the boundary of a cricket ground are perimeters.

games.title: True or false?
items: Perimeter is the distance all around a shape.
It is the length of the boundary.
The perimeter of a square is 4 × side.
A rectangle 5 cm by 2 cm has a perimeter of 10 cm.
5 + 2 + 5 + 2 = 14 cm. 10 is the area in square cm.
Perimeter can be measured in cm, m or km.
Perimeter is measured in square units.
Square units are for area. Perimeter is a length.

quiz.q: What is the perimeter of a rectangle 8 cm long and 5 cm wide?
quiz.mistake: Adds only two sides (13 cm) or multiplies (40)

quiz.q: What is the perimeter of a square with side 7 cm?
quiz.explain: A square has 4 equal sides: 4 × 7 = 28 cm.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies 7 × 7, which gives the area

quiz.q: A triangle has sides 5 cm, 6 cm and 7 cm. What is its perimeter?
quiz.explain: Add all three sides: 5 + 6 + 7 = 18 cm.
quiz.mistake: Adds only two sides, or multiplies

quiz.q: Nani's square table cloth has sides of 2 m. How much lace goes all around it?
quiz.explain: 4 sides of 2 m each: 4 × 2 = 8 m.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies 2 × 2, which is the area

quiz.q: A garden is 20 m long and 15 m wide. How long is the fence around it?
quiz.mistake: Adds only one length and one breadth

quiz.q: The perimeter of a square is 36 cm. How long is each side?
quiz.explain: A square has 4 equal sides: 36 ÷ 4 = 9 cm.
quiz.mistake: Divides by 2 instead of 4

quiz.q: A rectangle has a perimeter of 30 cm. Its length is 10 cm. What is its breadth?
quiz.explain: Length + breadth is half the perimeter: 30 ÷ 2 = 15. Breadth = 15 − 10 = 5 cm.
quiz.mistake: Takes 10 away from 30 without halving first

quiz.q: Which has the longer perimeter: a square with side 6 cm, or a rectangle 8 cm by 3 cm?
quiz.explain: Square: 4 × 6 = 24 cm. Rectangle: 2 × (8 + 3) = 22 cm. 24 > 22.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the shape with the longest side has the bigger perimeter

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'What is perimeter? How do I find it for my nest?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Perimeter is the length all around. Just add all the sides!
teach.nudge: Is perimeter inside or around a shape? What do I do with the sides?

learn.hook: Nani's quilt is made of little square patches. Count the patches and you know how much the quilt covers!
points: Area is the amount of surface a shape covers.
We measure area by counting unit squares. A 1 cm by 1 cm square has an area of 1 square cm (1 sq cm).
For a rectangle, area = length × breadth. 5 rows of 3 squares = 15 square units.
Two half squares make one full square.
Area uses square units: sq cm, sq m.

example.q: Nani's quilt has 6 patches along its length and 4 along its width. Each patch is 1 square unit. What is its area?

learn.reallife: Painters, carpet sellers and farmers all think about area.

games.title: Area or perimeter?
items: Border tape around a notice board

quiz.q: What is the area of a rectangle 5 cm long and 3 cm wide?
quiz.explain: Area = 5 × 3 = 15 sq cm.
quiz.mistake: Finds the perimeter (16 cm) instead of the area

quiz.q: What is the area of a square with side 6 cm?
quiz.explain: Area = 6 × 6 = 36 sq cm.
quiz.mistake: Finds the perimeter (4 × 6 = 24) instead

quiz.q: A shape covers 8 full squares and 4 half squares. What is its area?
quiz.explain: 4 half squares make 2 full squares. 8 + 2 = 10 square units.
quiz.mistake: Counts each half square as a full square

quiz.q: Nani's quilt has 7 rows of 5 patches. How many patches are there?
quiz.explain: 7 rows × 5 patches = 35.
quiz.mistake: Adds rows and patches instead of multiplying

quiz.q: Which unit should we use for the area of a notebook cover?
quiz.explain: Area is measured in square units. A notebook is small, so square centimetres fit.
quiz.mistake: Uses a unit of length for area

quiz.q: A room floor is 4 m by 3 m. Each tile covers 1 sq m. How many tiles cover the floor?
quiz.explain: Area = 4 × 3 = 12 sq m, so 12 tiles.
quiz.mistake: Adds length and breadth, or finds the perimeter

quiz.q: A rectangle has an area of 24 sq cm. Its length is 6 cm. What is its breadth?
quiz.explain: Length × breadth = area, so breadth = 24 ÷ 6 = 4 cm.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 6 from 24

quiz.q: Arjun says the area of a square with side 3 cm is 12 sq cm. What went wrong?
options: He found the perimeter, not the area
quiz.explain: 4 × 3 = 12 is the perimeter. The area is 3 × 3 = 9 sq cm.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up area and perimeter

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'What is area? How is it different from the border?'
teach.praise: Wow! Area is how much space a shape covers, counted in squares!
teach.nudge: Is area the edge or the inside? How do we count it?

learn.hook: Nani has 12 square patches. She can make a long thin quilt or a fat one. Same area, but will the border be the same?
points: Shapes with the same area can have different perimeters.
Shapes with the same perimeter can have different areas.
For 12 squares: 3 by 4 has perimeter 14, 2 by 6 has 16, 1 by 12 has 26.
Remember the units: perimeter in cm or m, area in sq cm or sq m.

example.q: Nani makes rectangles from 12 square patches (each side 1 unit). Find the perimeter of each.

learn.reallife: A farmer with a fixed length of fence can make fields of different sizes.

games.title: Same area, different borders
games.prompt: These rectangles each use 12 squares. Order them from smallest perimeter to largest

quiz.q: A 2 by 6 rectangle and a 3 by 4 rectangle are made of unit squares. What is the same about them?
quiz.explain: Both cover 12 squares (2 × 6 = 12, 3 × 4 = 12). Perimeters are 16 and 14.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the same area always means the same perimeter

quiz.q: What is the perimeter of a 1 by 12 rectangle?
quiz.mistake: Adds only one length and one breadth (13)

quiz.q: A 4 by 4 square and a 2 by 6 rectangle both have perimeter 16. Which has the bigger area?
quiz.explain: Square: 4 × 4 = 16 sq units. Rectangle: 2 × 6 = 12 sq units.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the same perimeter means the same area

quiz.q: Nani has 36 square patches. Which quilt shape uses all of them exactly?
quiz.explain: 6 × 6 = 36. The others give 35, 32 and 33.
quiz.mistake: Does not multiply to check

quiz.q: A rectangle has an area of 20 sq cm and a length of 5 cm. What is its perimeter?
quiz.explain: Breadth = 20 ÷ 5 = 4 cm. Perimeter = 2 × (5 + 4) = 18 cm.
quiz.mistake: Gives the area as the perimeter, or adds only two sides

quiz.q: A square has a perimeter of 20 cm. What is its area?
quiz.explain: Side = 20 ÷ 4 = 5 cm. Area = 5 × 5 = 25 sq cm.
quiz.mistake: Thinks area equals perimeter

quiz.q: A room is 5 m by 4 m. Carpet costs ₹100 for each square metre. How much does the carpet cost?
quiz.mistake: Uses the perimeter (18 m) instead of the area

quiz.q: Kabir doubles both sides of a 3 cm by 2 cm rectangle to make 6 cm by 4 cm. What happens to the area?
quiz.explain: Old area: 3 × 2 = 6. New area: 6 × 4 = 24. 24 is 4 times 6.
quiz.mistake: Thinks doubling the sides doubles the area

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'If two quilts cover the same area, do they need the same border?'
teach.praise: Oh! Same area can have a different border. Long thin quilts need more lace!
teach.nudge: Can the border change even if the area stays the same? Which shape needs more lace?

learn.hook: Clap once. That took about one second! How many claps fit in a minute?
points: A second is a very short time, about one clap.
60 seconds = 1 minute and 60 minutes = 1 hour.
Minutes to seconds: multiply by 60. 3 minutes = 3 × 60 = 180 seconds.
Seconds to minutes: divide by 60. 240 seconds = 4 minutes.
Mixed times: 2 minutes 15 seconds = 120 + 15 = 135 seconds.

example.q: Write 2 minutes 15 seconds in seconds.

learn.reallife: Races, cooking timers, cricket over timings and video clips use seconds and minutes.

quiz.q: How many seconds make 1 minute?
quiz.explain: 1 minute = 60 seconds.
quiz.mistake: Thinks time works in hundreds like money

quiz.q: How many seconds are there in 3 minutes?
quiz.explain: 3 × 60 = 180 seconds.
quiz.mistake: Adds 60 + 3, or uses 100 seconds in a minute

quiz.q: Write 2 minutes 15 seconds in seconds.
quiz.explain: 2 minutes = 120 seconds. 120 + 15 = 135 seconds.
quiz.mistake: Writes the numbers side by side (215)

quiz.q: 240 seconds is how many minutes?
quiz.explain: 240 ÷ 60 = 4 minutes.
quiz.mistake: Divides by 10 instead of 60

quiz.q: Which of these takes about one second?
quiz.explain: A single clap is very quick, about one second.
quiz.mistake: Has no feel for how short a second is

quiz.q: How many seconds are there in 1 hour?
quiz.explain: 1 hour = 60 minutes, and each minute is 60 seconds. 60 × 60 = 3,600.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies 60 × 6 instead of 60 × 60

quiz.q: 90 seconds is the same as…
quiz.explain: 90 = 60 + 30, so 90 seconds = 1 minute 30 seconds.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 1 minute is 100 seconds or 40 seconds

quiz.q: Riya held her breath for 45 seconds. Arjun held his for 1 minute. How many seconds longer was Arjun?
quiz.explain: 1 minute = 60 seconds. 60 − 45 = 15 seconds.
quiz.mistake: Takes 1 minute as 100 seconds, or adds

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How do I change minutes into seconds?'
teach.praise: Tick tock! Each minute has 60 seconds, so I multiply by 60!
teach.nudge: How many seconds are in one minute? What do I do with that number?

learn.hook: Your train leaves at 9:40 a.m. and reaches at 11:15 a.m. How long will you be looking out of the window?
points: Duration means how long something takes, from the start time to the end time.
Count on from the start: first to the next full hour, then whole hours, then the extra minutes.
a.m. is from midnight to noon. p.m. is from noon to midnight.
To find an end time, add the duration to the start time. 60 minutes make 1 hour.

example.q: A train leaves at 9:40 a.m. and arrives at 11:15 a.m. How long is the journey?

learn.reallife: Train timetables, school periods and TV shows all have start times, end times and durations.

items.text: From 3:00 p.m. to 3:45 p.m. is ___ minutes

quiz.q: A cricket match starts at 2:00 p.m. and ends at 5:30 p.m. How long does it last?
quiz.explain: 2:00 to 5:00 is 3 hours. 5:00 to 5:30 is 30 minutes more.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the extra 30 minutes

quiz.q: A film starts at 6:15 p.m. and lasts 2 hours 20 minutes. When does it end?
quiz.mistake: Adds only the hours

quiz.q: School runs from 8:00 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. How long is the school day?
quiz.explain: 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 noon is 4 hours. Noon to 1:30 p.m. is 1 hour 30 minutes. Total 5 hours 30 minutes.
quiz.mistake: Does 8 − 1 and gets confused crossing noon

quiz.q: Meena starts her homework at 4:50 p.m. and finishes at 5:25 p.m. How many minutes does she take?
quiz.explain: 4:50 to 5:00 is 10 minutes. 5:00 to 5:25 is 25 minutes. 10 + 25 = 35.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 50 − 25 or treats an hour as 100 minutes

quiz.q: Kabir's train leaves at 10:45 a.m. The journey takes 50 minutes. When does it arrive?
quiz.explain: 10:45 + 15 minutes = 11:00. 35 more minutes = 11:35 a.m.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 45 + 50 makes 95 minutes past 10

quiz.q: Joseph sleeps from 9:30 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. How long does he sleep?
quiz.explain: 9:30 p.m. to midnight is 2 hours 30 minutes. Midnight to 6:00 a.m. is 6 hours. Total 8 hours 30 minutes.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 9:30 − 6:00 without thinking about midnight

quiz.q: A bus ride takes 1 hour 15 minutes. How many minutes is that?
quiz.explain: 1 hour = 60 minutes. 60 + 15 = 75 minutes.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 1 hour is 100 minutes

quiz.q: Aisha practises the flute for 25 minutes every day for 4 days. How long does she practise in all?
quiz.explain: 25 × 4 = 100 minutes = 60 + 40 = 1 hour 40 minutes.
quiz.mistake: Changes 100 minutes into 1 hour 0 minutes, as if an hour were 100 minutes

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'My nap starts at 1:40 and ends at 2:15. How do I find how long I slept?'
teach.praise: Yawn! 1:40 to 2:00 is 20 minutes, then 15 more. 35 minutes of sleep!
teach.nudge: Where do I start counting? Is it easier to go to the next full hour first?

learn.hook: Ready, steady, go! In a race, the smallest time wins. Let's read stopwatches like a sports judge!
points: In a race, the runner who takes the least time is the fastest.
To compare times, write them in the same unit, usually seconds.
1 minute 5 seconds = 65 seconds, which is more than 58 seconds.
The difference between two times tells how much faster one runner is.

example.q: Riya ran in 52 seconds, Aisha in 1 minute 3 seconds and Harpreet in 49 seconds. Who won? Put them in order.
example.answer: Harpreet won; then Riya, then Aisha

learn.reallife: Sports days, the Olympics and car races measure winners in seconds and even parts of a second.

games.title: How long does it take?
items: a train ride from Delhi to Mumbai

games.title: True or false?
items: In a race, the runner with the least time wins.
A blink of an eye takes about 1 hour.
A blink takes much less than a second.

quiz.q: In a 50 m race, Arjun took 14 seconds, Kabir 12 seconds and Joseph 15 seconds. Who won?
quiz.explain: The smallest time wins. Kabir took only 12 seconds.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the biggest number wins

quiz.q: In that race, Kabir took 12 seconds and Joseph took 15 seconds. How many seconds faster was Kabir?
quiz.explain: 15 − 12 = 3 seconds.
quiz.mistake: Adds the times instead of finding the difference

quiz.q: Which is less time: 1 minute 5 seconds or 58 seconds?
quiz.explain: 1 minute 5 seconds = 65 seconds. 58 is less than 65.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 58 is more because 58 is bigger than 5

quiz.q: Four relay runners took 15, 14, 16 and 15 seconds. What was the team's total time?
quiz.explain: 15 + 14 + 16 + 15 = 60 seconds, which is exactly 1 minute.
quiz.mistake: Leaves out one runner

quiz.q: A stopwatch shows 1 minute 20 seconds. How many seconds is that?
quiz.explain: 1 minute = 60 seconds. 60 + 20 = 80 seconds.
quiz.mistake: Writes 1 and 20 side by side as 120

quiz.q: Meena ran the race in 58 seconds last week and 51 seconds today. By how many seconds did she improve?
quiz.explain: 58 − 51 = 7 seconds less, so she is 7 seconds faster.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two times

quiz.q: Riya ran in 50 seconds, Arjun in 47 seconds and Aisha in 53 seconds. Who came second?
quiz.explain: Order of times: 47 (Arjun), 50 (Riya), 53 (Aisha). Riya is second.
quiz.mistake: Orders from the biggest time

quiz.q: Harpreet's heart beats about 80 times in a minute. About how many times does it beat in 30 seconds?
quiz.explain: 30 seconds is half a minute. Half of 80 is 40.
quiz.mistake: Doubles instead of halving

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How do I know who is the fastest in a race?'
teach.praise: Zoom! The one who takes the least time wins. I'm racing the sparrows now!
teach.nudge: Does the fastest runner take more time or less time? How do I compare 1 minute 5 seconds and 58 seconds?

topics.title: Skip jumps on the number line

learn.hook: A frog jumps 3 steps at a time from 0. Will it ever land on 20? Let's hop along and see!
points: An animal that jumps the same size each time makes a skip pattern.
Jumping 3 at a time from 0 lands on 3, 6, 9, 12, … These are multiples of 3.
Landing spot = number of jumps × jump size. 6 jumps of 4 land on 24.
Starting at 2 and jumping 5 gives 2, 7, 12, 17, … (add 5 each time).
Jumping backwards means subtracting the jump size each time.

example.q: A frog jumps 4 steps at a time, starting at 0. Where is it after 6 jumps?

learn.reallife: Skip counting helps us count money in ₹5 or ₹10 notes and count pairs of socks quickly.

items.text: Jumps of 4 from 0: 4, 8, 12, ___
Jumps of 9 from 0: 9, 18, ___, 36
Start at 3, jumps of 10: 3, 13, 23, ___

games.title: True or false?
items: Jumps of 2 from 0 land only on even numbers.
Jumps of 5 from 0 can land on 34.
Jumps of 5 from 0 land only on numbers ending in 0 or 5.
Jumps of 10 from 0 always land on numbers ending in 0.
They land on 18 and then 21, skipping 20.
A frog jumping 4 at a time from 0 lands on 100.

quiz.q: A rabbit jumps 5 steps at a time from 0. Where is it after 4 jumps?
quiz.explain: 4 jumps × 5 = 20.
quiz.mistake: Adds 4 + 5 instead of multiplying

quiz.q: A frog jumps 3 steps at a time from 0. Which spot will it land on?
quiz.explain: 15 = 3 × 5, so the frog lands on 15. 10, 14 and 20 are not multiples of 3.
quiz.mistake: Picks a number that is near a landing spot

quiz.q: A grasshopper jumps 4 steps at a time from 0. How many jumps does it take to reach 28?
quiz.explain: 28 ÷ 4 = 7 jumps.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 4 from 28 instead of dividing

quiz.q: A kangaroo starts at 2 and jumps 5 each time: 2, 7, 12, 17, … Where does it land next?
quiz.mistake: Thinks it must land on multiples of 5, forgetting it started at 2

quiz.q: A squirrel starts at 30 and jumps back 6 each time. Where is it after 3 jumps?
quiz.mistake: Stops after 1 or 2 jumps

quiz.q: A frog jumps 7 steps at a time from 0. Will it land on 50?
options: No, 50 is not a multiple of 7
quiz.explain: 7 × 7 = 49 and 7 × 8 = 56. The frog jumps over 50.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 7 × 7 is 50

quiz.q: A deer leaps 6 steps at a time from 0. Where does it land on its 10th leap?
quiz.mistake: Adds 10 + 6 instead of multiplying

quiz.q: A frog starts at 1 and jumps 3 each time: 1, 4, 7, 10, 13, … Which of these will it land on?
quiz.explain: 13 + 3 = 16. 18, 20 and 21 are not in this pattern.
quiz.mistake: Picks a multiple of 3 (18 or 21), forgetting the frog started at 1

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'A frog jumps 4 at a time from 0. How do I know where it lands after 6 jumps?'
teach.praise: Ribbit! 6 jumps of 4 is 6 × 4 = 24. Multiply the jumps by the jump size!
teach.nudge: How big is each jump? How do I use the number of jumps?

learn.hook: A frog jumps 2 at a time and a rabbit jumps 3 at a time. Where will they land on the same spot? Let's race them!
points: A common multiple of two numbers is a multiple of both. 12 is a common multiple of 3 and 4.
Two animals starting at 0 land together on the common multiples of their jump sizes.
The first spot where they meet (after 0) is the smallest common multiple.
To find common multiples, list the multiples of each number and look for the numbers in both lists.

example.q: A frog jumps 3 at a time and a rabbit jumps 4 at a time, both from 0. Where do they first land on the same spot?

learn.reallife: If two friends visit the park every 2 and 3 days, common multiples tell when they meet.

quiz.q: A frog jumps 2 and a rabbit jumps 3, both from 0. Where do they first land on the same spot?
quiz.explain: Frog: 2, 4, 6. Rabbit: 3, 6. They first meet at 6.
quiz.mistake: Adds the jump sizes (5)

quiz.q: Which of these is a common multiple of 4 and 6?
quiz.explain: 12 is in both lists: 4 × 3 = 12 and 6 × 2 = 12. 16 is only a multiple of 4; 18 only of 6.
quiz.mistake: Picks a number that is a multiple of only one of them

quiz.q: What is the smallest common multiple of 5 and 10?
quiz.explain: 10 is a multiple of 5 (5 × 2) and of 10 (10 × 1).
quiz.mistake: Always multiplies the two numbers (50)

quiz.q: A frog jumps 4 and a rabbit jumps 6, both from 0. On a number line from 0 to 30, on how many spots (not counting 0) do both land?
quiz.explain: Common multiples of 4 and 6 up to 30 are 12 and 24. That is 2 spots.
quiz.mistake: Counts 0 as a landing spot, or misses 24

quiz.q: Which number is a common multiple of 3 and 5?
quiz.explain: 15 = 3 × 5. It is in both times tables. 20 and 25 are only multiples of 5; 18 only of 3.
quiz.mistake: Picks a multiple of just one number

quiz.q: Which list shows all the common multiples of 2 and 5 that are less than 40?
quiz.explain: A number that is a multiple of both 2 and 5 ends in 0: 10, 20, 30.
quiz.mistake: Includes 15, which is not even

quiz.q: A rabbit jumps 3 at a time and a kangaroo jumps 9 at a time, both from 0. Where do they first meet?
quiz.explain: 9 is a multiple of 3 (3 × 3), so they first meet at 9.
quiz.mistake: Always multiplies the jump sizes (27) or adds them (12)

quiz.q: Is 20 a common multiple of 4 and 6?
options: No, 20 is not a multiple of 6
No, 20 is not a multiple of 4
quiz.explain: 20 = 4 × 5, but 6 × 3 = 18 and 6 × 4 = 24, so 20 is not a multiple of 6.
quiz.mistake: Checks only one of the two numbers

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'What is a common multiple? Where will two jumping animals meet?'
teach.praise: Yippee! A common multiple is in both times tables. The first one is where they first meet!
teach.nudge: Must the number be in one list or both lists? Which one is the first meeting spot?

learn.hook: Two temple bells ring every 4 and 6 minutes. They ring together at 7:00. When will they ring together again?
points: When two things repeat at different gaps, they happen together at common multiples of the gaps.
The next time they happen together is the smallest common multiple.
If one number is a multiple of the other, the bigger number is the smallest common multiple: for 4 and 8 it is 8.
List multiples of the bigger number and check which is also a multiple of the smaller one. That is quick!

example.q: Bell A rings every 4 minutes and bell B every 6 minutes. Both ring at 7:00 a.m. When do they next ring together?
steps: Is 6 a multiple of 4? No. Is 12? Yes

learn.reallife: Bus timings, festival lights blinking at different speeds and buying packs to get equal numbers all use common multiples.

games.title: True or false?
items: The smallest common multiple of 4 and 8 is 32.
8 is already a multiple of 4, so the answer is 8.
Two numbers have many common multiples.
For 2 and 3: 6, 12, 18, 24, … they go on forever.
Every common multiple of 2 and 3 is also a multiple of 6.
Multiplying two numbers always gives their smallest common multiple.
For 6 and 9, 6 × 9 = 54, but 18 is smaller and works.
24 is a common multiple of 6 and 8.

quiz.q: Two bells ring every 6 minutes and every 8 minutes. They ring together at 9:00 a.m. After how many minutes do they ring together again?
quiz.explain: Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24. 24 is also a multiple of 6. So after 24 minutes.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies 6 × 8 (48), which is a common multiple but not the first

quiz.q: Riya visits the library every 4 days and Kabir every 6 days. They were both there today. In how many days will they meet there again?
quiz.explain: Multiples of 6: 6, 12. 12 is also a multiple of 4. They meet in 12 days.
quiz.mistake: Adds the gaps (10)

quiz.q: Laddoos come in boxes of 6 and pedas in boxes of 4. Meena wants the same number of each. What is the smallest number she can buy of each?
quiz.explain: 12 is the smallest number in both the 6 and 4 times tables. 2 boxes of laddoos and 3 boxes of pedas.
quiz.mistake: Adds 6 + 4, or multiplies to get 24

quiz.q: Two strings of Diwali lights blink every 3 seconds and every 5 seconds. They blink together now. After how many seconds will they blink together again?
quiz.explain: 3 and 5 have no common multiple smaller than 15. 15 = 3 × 5.
quiz.mistake: Adds 3 + 5

quiz.q: A blue bus leaves the depot every 10 minutes and a red bus every 15 minutes. Both leave at 8:00 a.m. When do they next leave together?
quiz.explain: Multiples of 15: 15, 30. 30 is a multiple of 10. 8:00 + 30 minutes = 8:30 a.m.
quiz.mistake: Adds 10 + 15 = 25 minutes

quiz.q: Arjun waters plant A every 2 days and plant B every 5 days. He waters both today. How many days until he waters both on the same day again?
quiz.explain: Multiples of 5: 5, 10. 10 is a multiple of 2. So 10 days.
quiz.mistake: Adds the gaps (7)

quiz.q: What is the smallest common multiple of 4 and 8?
quiz.explain: 8 is a multiple of 4 (4 × 2), so 8 is the smallest common multiple.
quiz.mistake: Always multiplies the two numbers

quiz.q: Aisha's cricket club meets every 3 days and her dance class every 9 days. Both are on Monday. After how many days are both on the same day again?
quiz.explain: 9 is a multiple of 3, so after 9 days.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies 3 × 9 (27) or adds them (12)

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'Two bells ring every 4 and every 6 minutes. How do I know when they ring together again?'
teach.praise: Ding dong! The first common multiple of 4 and 6 is 12. They ring together after 12 minutes!
teach.nudge: What should I list for each bell? Which number do I look for?

learn.hook: Imagine you are a bird flying over your town. What you see from up there is what a map shows!
points: A map is a drawing of a place as seen from above (a bird's-eye view).
A map is much smaller than the real place.
The key (legend) tells what each symbol on the map means.
Most maps have North at the top.
Grid maps use a letter for the column and a number for the row, like B4, to find places quickly.

example.q: On a grid map, columns are A to E (left to right) and rows are 1 to 5 (top to bottom). The temple is in column C, row 2. How do we name its square?
steps: Write the column letter first: C

learn.reallife: Maps help us find a shop in a mall, a platform at a railway station or a route on a phone.

games.title: True or false?
items: A map is a drawing of a place seen from above.
It is like a bird's-eye view.
A map key tells us what the symbols mean.
For example, 🌳 might stand for a park.
A map shows things bigger than they really are.
A map shrinks a place so it fits on paper.
On most maps, North is at the bottom.
On most maps, North is at the top.
Grid squares like B2 help us find places on a map.
The letter gives the column and the number gives the row.

quiz.q: On a map, what does the key (legend) tell us?
quiz.explain: The key explains the symbols, like 🏫 for a school.
quiz.mistake: Ignores the key and guesses what symbols mean

quiz.q: A map shows a place as it looks from…
quiz.explain: A map is a bird's-eye view, as if looking down from above.
quiz.mistake: Thinks of a picture taken from the side

quiz.q: On most maps, which direction is at the top?
quiz.explain: Most maps put North at the top.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the directions

quiz.q: On a grid map, the school is in column B, row 4. Which square is it in?
quiz.explain: Column letter first, then row number: B4.
quiz.mistake: Swaps the column and row

quiz.q: On a grid map, Arjun's house is in A1 and the market is in A4, in the same column. How many squares down is the market from his house?
quiz.explain: From row 1 to row 4 is 4 − 1 = 3 squares.
quiz.mistake: Counts the starting square too

quiz.q: A map shows a whole city on one page. Compared with the real city, the map is…
quiz.explain: A map shrinks the real place so it fits on paper.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a map is drawn at real size

quiz.q: Which is the best landmark to tell a friend the way to your house?
options: A big red temple at the corner
quiz.explain: A landmark should be big and stay in one place. Clouds, bicycles and dogs move!
quiz.mistake: Picks something that moves away

quiz.q: On a grid map, rows are numbered 1 at the top to 5 at the bottom. The park is in C3. Which square is just above it?
quiz.explain: Moving up one row in the same column: row 3 → row 2. So C2.
quiz.mistake: Moves along the row instead of up, or goes down

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'What is a map? How do I know what the little pictures mean?'
teach.praise: Wow! A map is a bird's-eye drawing, and the key tells what each symbol means. Just like my view!
teach.nudge: From where is a map drawn? What tells me the meaning of each symbol?

learn.hook: The sun rises in the East every morning. Can you use it to find North, South and West? Let's become explorers!
points: The four main directions are North, South, East and West.
If you face North, East is on your right, West is on your left and South is behind you.
The sun rises in the East and sets in the West.
Between the main directions are North-East, North-West, South-East and South-West.
A right turn is a quarter turn clockwise. A left turn is a quarter turn anticlockwise.

example.q: Meena faces North. She turns right, and then turns right again. Which way is she facing now?

learn.reallife: Taxi drivers, pilots, ship captains and scouts all use directions.

items.text: Facing North, your left hand points ___
The opposite of South is ___
The sun sets in the ___
Between South and West is ___

games.title: True or false?
items: If you face East, North is on your left.
Facing East, turning left (anticlockwise) takes you to North.
If you face South, East is on your right.
Facing South, West is on your right and East is on your left.
Turning right two times from North makes you face South.
North-West is between North and West.
Its name tells you: North + West.
Turning from East to South is a left turn.
East to South is clockwise, so it is a right turn.

quiz.q: You are facing North. Which direction is on your right?
quiz.explain: Facing North, East is on your right.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up left and right

quiz.q: Kabir faces East and turns left. Which way does he face now?
quiz.explain: A left turn is anticlockwise. From East, anticlockwise goes to North.
quiz.mistake: Turns right instead of left

quiz.q: In which direction does the sun rise?
quiz.explain: The sun rises in the East every morning.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up sunrise and sunset

quiz.q: Arjun walks 3 blocks North, then 2 blocks East, then 3 blocks South. Where is he now compared with his start?
quiz.explain: The 3 blocks North and 3 blocks South cancel out. He is 2 blocks East of his start.
quiz.mistake: Adds all the blocks together

quiz.q: Harpreet faces West and turns right. Which way does she face now?
quiz.explain: A right turn is clockwise. From West, clockwise goes to North.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a right turn always leads to East

quiz.q: Which direction is halfway between North and East?
quiz.explain: Halfway between North and East is North-East.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the names of the in-between directions

quiz.q: Riya walks 4 blocks East and then 4 blocks West. How many blocks is she from where she started?
quiz.explain: East and West are opposite. 4 − 4 = 0, so she is back at the start.
quiz.mistake: Adds the blocks instead of seeing the walks cancel

quiz.q: Joseph faces North and turns until he faces South. How many degrees did he turn?
quiz.explain: North to South is a half turn, which is 180°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks it is a quarter turn

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'I am facing North. Where are East, West and South?'
teach.praise: Hooray! East on my right, West on my left and South behind me. Now I won't get lost!
teach.nudge: Which direction is on my right hand? Which one is behind me?

learn.hook: How can a whole state fit on one page? The secret is the map scale!
points: A map scale tells how much real distance 1 cm on the map stands for.
If 1 cm = 5 km, then 4 cm on the map is 4 × 5 = 20 km in real life.
Real distance = map length × the scale distance.
Map length = real distance ÷ the scale distance.
Always write the units: cm on the map, m or km in real life.

example.q: On a map, 1 cm stands for 5 km. Two towns are 4 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they really?

learn.reallife: Road atlases, school plans and phone maps all use scales. Zooming in on a phone changes the scale!

items.q: 1 cm = 2 km. 10 km in real life = ? cm on the map

quiz.q: A map scale is 1 cm = 10 km. Two villages are 3 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they really?
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of multiplying

quiz.q: On Riya's school map, 1 cm = 100 m. The playground is 7 cm from the gate on the map. How far is it really?
quiz.mistake: Adds a zero too many or too few

quiz.q: A map scale is 1 cm = 2 km. Two towns are 12 km apart. How far apart are they on the map?
quiz.explain: Each 2 km takes 1 cm. 12 ÷ 2 = 6 cm.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies when it should divide

quiz.q: On Aisha's map, 1 cm = 50 km. Two cities are 4 cm apart. How far apart are they really?
quiz.mistake: Adds 4 + 50

quiz.q: A plan of a cricket ground uses 1 cm = 5 m. The ground is 9 cm long on the plan. How long is it really?
quiz.mistake: Adds the numbers instead of multiplying

quiz.q: Map A uses 1 cm = 1 km. Map B uses 1 cm = 2 km. Both show the same city on the same paper. On which map does the city look bigger?
quiz.explain: On Map A each km takes 1 cm. On Map B each km takes only half a cm. So the city looks bigger on Map A.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the bigger number in the scale makes things look bigger

quiz.q: A map scale is 1 cm = 25 km. A route has three parts of 2 cm, 3 cm and 1 cm on the map. How long is the real route?
quiz.explain: Total map length: 2 + 3 + 1 = 6 cm. Real: 6 × 25 = 150 km.
quiz.mistake: Gives the map length in cm, or adds 25 only once

quiz.q: A map scale is 1 cm = 20 m. A park is 80 m wide. How wide is it on the map?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies instead of dividing

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How can a big city fit on a small map? What is a scale?'
teach.praise: Clever! Each cm on the map stands for a real distance, so I multiply to find how far!
teach.nudge: What does 1 cm on the map stand for? How do I find the real distance?

learn.hook: Can one little mango picture stand for 5 mangoes? In a pictograph, it can!
points: A pictograph shows data using pictures or symbols.
The key tells how many things one symbol stands for, like 🥭 = 5 mangoes.
To read it, multiply the number of symbols by the key.
Half a symbol stands for half the key number.
Choose a key that keeps the pictures easy to draw and count.

example.q: Key: 🍎 = 10 apples. A shop's row shows 🍎🍎🍎🍎 and half an 🍎. How many apples?

learn.reallife: Pictographs are used in newspapers, school charts and posters to show data in a fun way.

items.text: 6 sunny days are shown by ___ ☀️
4 ☀️ stand for ___ sunny days
Half a ☀️ stands for ___ sunny day

quiz.q: Key: 🍎 = 10 apples. A shop's row shows 🍎🍎🍎🍎. How many apples does the shop have?
quiz.explain: 4 symbols × 10 = 40 apples.
quiz.mistake: Counts the symbols but forgets the key

quiz.q: Key: ⭐ = 4 children. A row shows 3 and a half ⭐. How many children is that?
quiz.explain: 3 stars = 12 children. Half a star = 2 children. 12 + 2 = 14.
quiz.mistake: Ignores the half symbol, or counts it as a full one

quiz.q: Key: 🏏 = 10 runs. Kabir has 🏏🏏🏏🏏🏏🏏 and Joseph has 🏏🏏🏏. How many more runs did Kabir score?
quiz.mistake: Gives the difference in symbols (3) and forgets the key

quiz.q: Key: 🙂 = 5 children. How many 🙂 are needed to show 35 children?
quiz.explain: 35 ÷ 5 = 7 symbols.
quiz.mistake: Draws one symbol for each child

quiz.q: Why does a pictograph have a key?
options: So we know how many each symbol stands for
quiz.explain: Without the key we cannot tell if one symbol means 1, 5 or 10 things.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the symbols always mean 1 each

quiz.q: Key: 📚 = 20 books. The library row shows 📚📚 and half a 📚. How many books?
quiz.mistake: Forgets the half symbol

quiz.q: A pictograph will show 200, 350 and 500 visitors at a mela. Which key is the best choice?
quiz.explain: With 50, the rows need 4, 7 and 10 symbols. Easy to draw and read!
quiz.mistake: Picks a key that needs hundreds of symbols or does not divide the numbers

quiz.q: Key: 🌸 = 6 flowers. Meena picked 24 flowers. How many 🌸 symbols show this?
quiz.explain: 24 ÷ 6 = 4 symbols.
quiz.mistake: Uses the key number as the answer

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'In a pictograph, how do I know how many things one picture means?'
teach.praise: Yay! Read the key, then multiply the symbols by it. Easy-peasy!
teach.nudge: What part of the pictograph tells me what a symbol is worth? What do I do then?

learn.hook: Which fruit does your class love most? A bar graph shows the winner in one look!
points: A bar graph uses bars of different lengths to show data.
The longer or taller the bar, the bigger the number it shows.
The scale on the side tells what each line stands for, like 1 line = 2 children.
All bars should be the same width with equal gaps between them.
Bars can go up (vertical) or across (horizontal).

example.q: On a bar graph each line stands for 2 children. The Mango bar reaches 6 lines. How many children chose mango?

learn.reallife: Cricket scorecards on TV, rainfall charts and school results often use bar graphs.

games.title: Fewest to most votes
games.prompt: Favourite game votes: Kabaddi 9, Cricket 15, Football 11, Kho-kho 6. Order the bars from shortest to tallest

games.title: True or false?
items: In a bar graph, all bars should be the same width.
Only the length should change, so the graph is fair.
The longest bar shows the smallest number.
The longest bar shows the biggest number.
We need the scale to read the numbers on a bar graph.
The scale tells what each line stands for.
Bars can be drawn going across, not only up.
Horizontal bar graphs work the same way.
If 1 line = 5, a bar 4 lines tall shows 4.

quiz.q: Favourite fruits in Class 5: Mango 12, Banana 8, Apple 5, Grapes 10. Which fruit has the tallest bar?
quiz.explain: Mango has the biggest number, 12, so its bar is tallest.
quiz.mistake: Picks the fruit with the shortest bar

quiz.q: Using the same fruit graph (Mango 12, Banana 8), how many more children chose Mango than Banana?
quiz.mistake: Adds the two bars

quiz.q: In the fruit graph (Mango 12, Banana 8, Apple 5, Grapes 10), how many children voted in all?
quiz.mistake: Leaves out one bar

quiz.q: On a bar graph, each line stands for 2 children. A bar reaches 7 lines. How many children does it show?
quiz.explain: 7 × 2 = 14 children.
quiz.mistake: Reads the number of lines and forgets the scale

quiz.q: Runs in each over: Over 1 = 6, Over 2 = 10, Over 3 = 4, Over 4 = 12. Which over had the most runs?
quiz.explain: Over 4 has the tallest bar with 12 runs.
quiz.mistake: Picks the over with the shortest bar

quiz.q: Using the runs graph (6, 10, 4 and 12 runs), how many runs were scored in all 4 overs?
quiz.mistake: Makes an adding slip or misses one over

quiz.q: Rainy days: June 8, July 15, August 12, September 6. Which month had the fewest rainy days?
quiz.explain: September has the shortest bar, 6 days.
quiz.mistake: Picks the month with the most rain

quiz.q: What does a taller bar on a bar graph tell us?
options: There is more of that thing
There is less of that thing
quiz.explain: Bar height shows the number. Taller means more.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the height has no meaning

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How do I read a bar graph?'
teach.praise: Super! Taller bars mean more, and the scale tells me the exact number!
teach.nudge: What does the height of a bar show? What tells me what each line is worth?

learn.hook: Class 5 did a survey: how do you come to school? Let's be data detectives and find the story in the numbers!
points: Tally marks are drawn in bundles of 5 (four lines and one across) to count quickly.
From data we can find the most, the least, the total and the difference.
We can also find fractions of the data: 20 out of 40 is half.
Only say what the data really shows. Do not guess things it does not tell.

example.q: 40 children answered: 20 walk, 12 come by bus, 8 cycle. What fraction walk? How many more walk than cycle?
example.answer: Half walk; 12 more walk than cycle

learn.reallife: Schools, shops and doctors collect data to make good decisions.

games.title: Data: dogs 10, cats 6, fish 4
buckets: Can be answered from the data
items: How many more dogs than cats?
Which pet is the least common?

items.q: Bars of 12 and 7: how many more?

quiz.q: A tally shows two bundles of five and 3 more lines. What number is that?
quiz.mistake: Counts each bundle as 1

quiz.q: 40 children were asked how they come to school. 20 walk. What fraction of the children walk?
quiz.mistake: Writes the number who walk over the number who don't (20/20)

quiz.q: In the same survey, 20 children walk and 8 cycle. How many more walk than cycle?
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of finding the difference

quiz.q: Temperatures this week: Mon 30°, Tue 32°, Wed 29°, Thu 33°. Which day was the hottest?
quiz.explain: 33° is the highest, so Thursday was the hottest.
quiz.mistake: Picks the coolest day

quiz.q: Favourite part of Diwali: Sweets 15, Diyas 12, Rangoli 9, Lights 4. Which statement is TRUE?
options: Lights are more popular than Diyas
Rangoli and Diyas got the same votes
quiz.explain: 15 is the biggest number, so Sweets got the most votes.
quiz.mistake: Reads the numbers carelessly

quiz.q: In that Diwali survey (15, 12, 9 and 4 votes), how many children voted in all?
quiz.mistake: Leaves out the smallest number

quiz.q: Books read this month: Riya 5, Arjun 8, Meena 6, Kabir 5. How many children read more than 5 books?
quiz.explain: Arjun (8) and Meena (6) read more than 5. Riya and Kabir read exactly 5, which is not more than 5.
quiz.mistake: Counts children who read exactly 5 as 'more than 5'

quiz.q: In a quiz, Team A scored 45 and Team B scored 60. By how many points did Team B win?
quiz.explain: 60 − 45 = 15 points.
quiz.mistake: Adds the scores

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'What can we learn from a table of numbers?'
teach.praise: Wow! Data tells us the most, the least, the total and how many more. I'm a data detective now!
teach.nudge: What questions can I answer from the numbers? Can I find the biggest and the total?
